knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization-form MIQP, classified by global quadratic curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n,p\in\mathbb N\), \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\). A convex mixed-integer quadratic program in minimization form is
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x:Ax\le b,\ x_i\in\mathbb Z\ \text{for every }i\in I\right\}.\]
Its objective and the feasible region of its continuous relaxation are convex, although its mixed-integer feasible set is generally nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex MIQP minimizes a positive-semidefinite quadratic over linear constraints and prescribed integer variables; its continuous relaxation is convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex MIQP

Its objective is concave on \(\mathbb R^n\). Unless the objective is affine when restricted to the continuous feasible region, its continuous relaxation is not a convex optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under minimization, a concave-objective MIQP has a negative-semidefinite quadratic objective; unless that objective is affine on the continuous feasible region, the continuous relaxation is not a convex optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Concave-Objective MIQP

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n,p\in\mathbb N\), \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\). An indefinite mixed-integer quadratic program in minimization form is
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x:Ax\le b,\ x_i\in\mathbb Z\ \text{for every }i\in I\right\},\]
where \(Q\) has at least one positive and at least one negative eigenvalue. Its quadratic objective is neither convex nor concave on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An indefinite MIQP has a symmetric objective matrix with both positive and negative eigenvalues, making its quadratic objective neither convex nor concave on the ambient real space.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n,m,p\in\mathbb N\), let \(Q_j\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c_j\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(d_j\in\mathbb R\) for \(j=0,\ldots,m\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), and let \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\). A convex mixed-integer quadratically constrained program in minimization form is
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12x^\top Q_0x+c_0^\top x\quad\text{subject to}\quad \tfrac12x^\top Q_jx+c_j^\top x\le d_j\ \ (j=1,\ldots,m),\quad Ax\le b,\quad x_i\in\mathbb Z\ \ (i\in I).\]
Dropping the integrality restrictions yields a convex quadratically constrained program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex MIQCP minimizes a positive-semidefinite quadratic subject to positive-semidefinite quadratic inequalities, linear constraints, and prescribed integer variables; its continuous relaxation is convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex MIQCP

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n,m,p\in\mathbb N\), let \(Q_j\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, \(c_j\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(d_j\in\mathbb R\) for \(j=0,\ldots,m\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), and let \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\). A nonconvex mixed-integer quadratically constrained program is an MIQCP
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12x^\top Q_0x+c_0^\top x\quad\text{subject to}\quad \tfrac12x^\top Q_jx+c_j^\top x\le d_j\ \ (j=1,\ldots,m),\quad Ax\le b,\quad x_i\in\mathbb Z\ \ (i\in I),\]
whose continuous relaxation is nonconvex. A matrix \(Q_0\not\succeq0\) or \(Q_j\not\succeq0\) signals nonconvex curvature on \(\mathbb R^n\), but that matrix condition alone does not prove that the relaxation is nonconvex because domain restriction, redundancy, or the geometry of a particular sublevel set may matter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonconvex MIQCP is an MIQCP whose continuous relaxation is nonconvex. A non-positive-semidefinite objective or constraint matrix signals nonconvex curvature but does not by itself establish nonconvexity of the entire relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex MIQCP

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic mixed-integer quadratically constrained quadratic program without curvature restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n,m,p\in\mathbb N\) with \(m\ge1\), let \(Q_j\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, \(c_j\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(d_j\in\mathbb R\) for \(j=0,\ldots,m\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), and let \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\). A mixed-integer quadratically constrained quadratic program is
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12x^\top Q_0x+c_0^\top x\quad\text{subject to}\quad \tfrac12x^\top Q_jx+c_j^\top x\le d_j\ \ (j=1,\ldots,m),\quad Ax\le b,\quad x_i\in\mathbb Z\ \ (i\in I).\]
No definiteness restriction is imposed on the quadratic matrices; convex and nonconvex subclasses are determined from the objective and feasible geometry of the continuous relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed-integer QCQP has a quadratic objective, at least one quadratic constraint, and prescribed integer variables, with no general definiteness requirement on its quadratic matrices.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer QCQP
Quadratic-Equality Mixed-Integer Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed-integer models containing at least one genuine quadratic equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A quadratic-equality mixed-integer model contains constraints
\[x^\top Q_jx+c_j^\top x=d_j\quad(j\in E),\qquad x_i\in\mathbb Z\quad(i\in I),\]
possibly together with additional linear or quadratic inequalities, where \(E\ne\varnothing\) and at least one equality has \(Q_j\ne0\). A genuine quadratic equality is generally nonconvex because it is the intersection of opposite quadratic inequalities; affine or domain-degenerate cases are exceptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This model class imposes at least one nonaffine quadratic equality together with integer restrictions; such equalities generally make the continuous feasible set nonconvex.
assumptions_latex: \(E\ne\varnothing\) and \(Q_j=Q_j^\top\) for every \(j\in E\).
\(Q_j\ne0\) for at least one \(j\in E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model contains a genuine quadratic equality and is generally nonconvex after integrality is relaxed.

notation.meaning: index set of quadratic equality constraints

knowledge_statements.title: Unconstrained Binary Quadratic Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical QUBO formulation, allowing constants to be absorbed into the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An unconstrained binary quadratic model, or QUBO, is
\[\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}\ x^\top Qx+c^\top x+\alpha,\]
where \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\). It has no constraints beyond binary membership. Because \(x_i^2=x_i\), diagonal quadratic terms may equivalently be absorbed into the linear coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A QUBO minimizes a quadratic polynomial over binary vectors with no constraints other than each variable being zero or one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimization problem is unconstrained apart from \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), and diagonal terms can be represented linearly.

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Binary Quadratic Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary quadratic optimization over an explicitly restricted binary feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A constrained binary quadratic model is
\[\min_{x\in X}\ x^\top Qx+c^\top x+\alpha,\qquad X=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:g_r(x)\le0\ (r=1,\ldots,p),\ h_s(x)=0\ (s=1,\ldots,q)\},\]
where \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) and the constraint functions are specified linear or quadratic polynomials. Unlike QUBO, feasibility is restricted by at least one explicit constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained binary quadratic model optimizes a quadratic polynomial over binary vectors satisfying one or more explicit linear or quadratic constraints.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_r\) and \(h_s\) is linear or quadratic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible set \(X\) is an explicitly constrained subset of \(\{0,1\}^n\).

knowledge_statements.title: General-Integer Quadratic Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic optimization with bounded or otherwise constrained general-integer variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A general-integer quadratic model has the form
\[\min_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}\ \tfrac12z^\top Qz+c^\top z\quad\text{subject to}\quad Az\le b,\ \ell\le z\le u,\]
where integer variables may take more than two admissible values. The matrix \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) may be positive semidefinite, negative semidefinite, or indefinite; its curvature does not alter the general-integer domain classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general-integer quadratic model optimizes a quadratic function over integer variables that need not be binary, usually subject to bounds and linear constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(z\in\mathbb Z^n\).
At least one variable has more than two admissible integer values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model is quadratic over a general-integer, rather than purely binary, feasible domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Binary–Continuous Product Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed-domain models containing products of binary and continuous variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A binary–continuous product model contains at least one relation
\[w=xy,\qquad y\in\{0,1\},\qquad L\le x\le U,\]
where \(x\) is continuous and \(w\) represents their bilinear product. With finite bounds, this graph is represented exactly over the binary domain by
\[Ly\le w\le Uy,\qquad x-U(1-y)\le w\le x-L(1-y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: These models contain a product of a binary variable and a bounded continuous variable; four linear inequalities represent the product exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in[L,U]\subset\mathbb R\) with finite \(L\le U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The four displayed linear inequalities are equivalent to \(w=xy\) on the stated mixed domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer–Continuous Product Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed-domain models containing products of general-integer and continuous variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An integer–continuous product model contains at least one relation
\[w=zx,\qquad z\in\mathbb Z\cap[\ell,u],\qquad x\in[L,U]\subset\mathbb R,\]
where \(z\) is a general-integer variable and \(x\) is continuous. The relation is bilinear and generally nonconvex in the continuous relaxation. If \(\ell\) and \(u\) are finite, encoding \(z\) with binary variables reduces the product to finitely many binary–continuous products.

children.title: Separable Quadratic Structure
children.top_down_role: Quadratic models whose variable interactions decompose into independent scalar components.

assumptions_latex: The quadratic function is defined on \(\mathbb R^n\).
The matrix \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) is symmetric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quadratic term is separable exactly when \(Q\) is diagonal in the stated coordinate system.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-wise separability in the given variables, not separability after an arbitrary rotation.

source_refs.locator: 4.4 DC Representation of Separable Functions p. 110

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A quadratic function \(f(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\) has separable quadratic structure in coordinates \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) if there exist univariate quadratic functions \(f_i\) and a constant \(d\) such that \[f(x)=d+\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i).\] For symmetric \(Q\), this holds if and only if \(Q_{ij}=0\) whenever \(i\ne j\). Equivalently, \[f(x)=d+\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl(q_i x_i^2+c_i x_i\bigr).\] Integrality restrictions on selected coordinates do not alter this algebraic definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic function is coordinate-wise separable precisely when it has no cross-products, equivalently when its symmetric quadratic matrix is diagonal.
knowledge_statements.title: Separable Quadratic Structure

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4 DC Representation of Separable Functions p. 110

children.title: Block-Quadratic Structure
children.top_down_role: Quadratic models organized into interacting variable blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Quadratic Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block structure is relative to a fixed partition of the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), and let \(\{B_1,\ldots,B_k\}\) be a partition of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). A quadratic function \(f(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\) has block-quadratic structure for this partition if it decomposes as \[f(x)=d+\sum_{r=1}^k f_r(x_{B_r}),\] where every \(f_r\) is quadratic. This holds if and only if \(Q_{B_rB_s}=0\) for all distinct \(r,s\); equivalently, after a simultaneous permutation of its rows and columns, \(Q\) is block diagonal. Blocks may contain continuous, integer, or mixed-domain coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic function is block-quadratic for a fixed partition when no quadratic cross-term joins different blocks; equivalently, its symmetric matrix is block diagonal after permutation.
assumptions_latex: The vector satisfies \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).
The index sets \(B_1,\ldots,B_k\) form a partition of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
The matrix satisfies \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The function is block-quadratic for the partition exactly when \(Q_{B_rB_s}=0\) for every \(r\ne s\).

notation.meaning: quadratic matrix block with row indices B_r and column indices B_s

assumptions_latex: The matrix \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) represents the quadratic term in fixed coordinates.
The interaction graph has vertex set \(\{1,ldots,n\}\) and edge \(\{i,j\}\) exactly when \(i\ne j\) and \(Q_{ij}\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The connected components are the unique finest nonempty blocks yielding block separability; any admissible block partition coarsens them.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes exactly where a proposed partition ceases to provide additive block separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) be the connected components of \(G(Q)\). Then \(Q_{C_rC_s}=0\) for \(r\ne s\), so the quadratic function is block separable over these components. Moreover, a partition \(\{B_1,\ldots,B_k\}\) yields block separability if and only if every interaction edge has both endpoints in one block, equivalently each \(C_r\) is contained in some \(B_s\). children.title: Bilinear Interaction Structure
children.top_down_role: Cross-products between distinct variable groups in quadratic models.

assumptions_latex: The variables are partitioned as \(x\in\mathbb R^p\) and \(y\in\mathbb R^q\).
The coefficient matrix satisfies \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The term \(x^{\mathsf T}Ay\) is affine in either block when the other block is fixed, and its nonzero entries identify cross-block interactions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block bilinear terms, including rectangular cross-interaction matrices.

source_refs.locator: Part I. Biconvex and Bilinear Problems

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A bilinear interaction between blocks \(x\) and \(y\) is a function \[b(x,y)=x^{\mathsf T}Ay=\sum_{i=1}^p\sum_{j=1}^q A_{ij}x_i y_j.\] For each fixed \(y\), the mapping \(x\mapsto b(x,y)\) is linear, and for each fixed \(x\), the mapping \(y\mapsto b(x,y)\) is linear. In a symmetric quadratic representation of \((x,y)\), this interaction corresponds to the off-diagonal blocks \(A/2\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}/2\). An entry \(A_{ij}\ne0\) records an interaction between \(x_i\) and \(y_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bilinear interaction is a cross-block term x-transpose-A-y. It is linear in either block when the other is fixed, with nonzeros of A marking interactions.

The function \(f:X\times Y\tob R\) is finite-valued.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard two-block, finite-dimensional biconvexity on a Cartesian product.

source_refs.locator: Part I. Biconvex and Bilinear Problems

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) has biconvex block structure on \(X\times Y\) if, for every fixed \(y\in Y\), the slice \(x\mapsto f(x,y)\) is convex on \(X\), and, for every fixed \(x\in X\), the slice \(y\mapsto f(x,y)\) is convex on \(Y\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact characterization for an unconstrained two-block quadratic on full Euclidean spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^p\), \(y\in\mathbb R^q\), \(P\in\mathbb S^p\), \(R\in\mathbb S^q\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}\), \(a\in\mathbb R^p\), \(b\in\mathbb R^q\), and \(d\in\mathbb R\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every real scalar quadratic polynomial has a representation \[q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d,\qquad Q\in\mathbb S^n.\] If an initial coefficient matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is not symmetric, then \(x^{\mathsf T}Ax=x^{\mathsf T}Qx\) for \[Q=\tfrac12\bigl(A+A^{\mathsf T}\bigr),\] because the skew-symmetric part contributes zero. knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order-Cone Quadratic Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard second-order-cone representation of a positive-semidefinite quadratic epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), choose \(R\) such that \(Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\), and let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(t\in\mathbb R\). The convex quadratic inequality \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx\le t\) is equivalent to the standard second-order-cone constraint \(\left\|(2Rx,t-1)\right\|_2\le t+1\). Indeed, the cone constraint also implies \(t\ge0\), and its squared form reduces exactly to \(\|Rx\|_2^2\le t\). Hence any positive-semidefinite quadratic epigraph admits this exact second-order-cone representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factoring Q as RᵀR converts xᵀQx≤t exactly into one standard second-order-cone constraint.

\(Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\)

\(Q=R^\top R\)

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal Curvature Redistribution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact diagonal shifting on binary coordinates that produces a convex quadratic matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) index binary variables, and let \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(d_i=0\) for \(i\notin B\). With \(D=\operatorname{Diag}(d)\), every \(x\) satisfying \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) for \(i\in B\) obeys \[x^\top Qx+c^\top x=x^\top(Q-D)x+(c+d)^\top x.\] Consequently, any such \(d\) with \(Q-D\succeq0\) gives an exact convex-quadratic reformulation on the mixed-binary feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary identities permit diagonal curvature to move from the quadratic matrix into the linear term; a positive-semidefinite residual matrix yields an exact convex reformulation.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\)
\(d_i=0\) for \(i\notin B\)

knowledge_statements.title: Eigenvector Reformulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral separation of negative curvature into scalar quadratic directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) have spectral decomposition \(Q=Q_+-\sum_{k=1}^r\lambda_kv_kv_k^\top\), where \(Q_+\succeq0\), \(\lambda_k>0\), and the \(v_k\) are orthonormal negative-curvature eigenvectors. Introducing \(z_k=v_k^\top x\) gives the exact representation \[x^\top Qx=x^\top Q_+x-\sum_{k=1}^r\lambda_kz_k^2,\qquad z_k=v_k^\top x.\] Hence all nonconvex curvature is isolated in \(r\) one-dimensional concave quadratic terms while the remaining quadratic form is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spectral decomposition isolates each negative eigenvalue as a scalar concave square, leaving a positive-semidefinite quadratic remainder.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\)
\(Q=Q_+-\sum_{k=1}^r\lambda_kv_kv_k^\top\) with \(Q_+\succeq0\) and \(\lambda_k>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\top Qx=x^\top Q_+x-\sum_{k=1}^r\lambda_kz_k^2\) under \(z_k=v_k^\top x\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed spectral decomposition and scalar-direction representation are mathematically correct, and representation fits the leaf. No source establishes that this is the intended eigenvector-reformulation variant in the mixed-integer quadratic context.

knowledge_statements.title: SDP-Selected Quadratic Convex Reformulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite selection of an exact diagonal shift for mixed-binary quadratic objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), binary index set \(B\), and weights \(w_i>0\), solve \[\max_d\ \sum_{i\in B}w_id_i\quad\text{subject to}\quad Q-\operatorname{Diag}(d)\succeq0,\qquad d_i=0\ \text{for}\ i\notin B.\] For an optimizer \(d^*\), replace \(x^\top Qx+c^\top x\) by \(x^\top(Q-\operatorname{Diag}(d^*))x+(c+d^*)^\top x\). The replacement is exact whenever \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) for \(i\in B\), and its quadratic matrix is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SDP chooses a weighted diagonal shift that preserves binary objective values and leaves a convex quadratic matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\)
\(w_i>0\) for \(i\in B\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q-\operatorname{Diag}(d^*)\succeq0\) and the shifted objective equals the original objective on the mixed-binary domain

The particular weighted maximization model is specialized and uncited. children.title: McCormick Envelope Family
children.top_down_role: Envelope families for bounded scalar product graphs.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Bilinear Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-hull description of one bounded continuous bilinear graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite bounds \(l_x<u_x\) and \(l_y<u_y\), the convex hull of \(\{(x,y,z):l_x\le x\le u_x,\ l_y\le y\le u_y,\ z=xy\}\) is described by the bounds and \[z\ge l_xy+l_yx-l_xl_y,\qquad z\ge u_xy+u_yx-u_xu_y,\] \[z\le u_xy+l_yx-u_xl_y,\qquad z\le l_xy+u_yx-l_xu_y.\] These four inequalities are the McCormick envelope of \(z=xy\) over the rectangle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Four affine McCormick inequalities give the exact convex hull of a bilinear graph over a bounded rectangle.
assumptions_latex: \((x,y)\in[l_x,u_x]\times[l_y,u_y]\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed four inequalities describe \(\operatorname{conv}\{(x,y,xy)\}\) over the rectangle

knowledge_statements.title: Binary–Continuous Product Hulls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ideal linear formulation for a product of one binary and one bounded continuous variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\{0,1\}\), \(l\le y\le u\), and \(z=xy\), where \(l,u\in\mathbb R\) are finite. The convex hull in \((x,y,z)\)-space is given by \[0\le x\le1,\qquad l\le y\le u,\] \[lx\le z\le ux,\qquad y-u(1-x)\le z\le y-l(1-x).\] Thus relaxing only the integrality of \(x\) in this extended formulation yields the exact convex hull of the binary–continuous product graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Four linear inequalities, together with bounds, form the exact convex hull of a bounded continuous variable multiplied by a binary variable.
assumptions_latex: \(l\le y\le u\)
\(l,u\in\mathbb R\) are finite
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed linear system equals \(\operatorname{conv}\{(x,y,xy):x\in\{0,1\},\ l\le y\le u\}\)

notation.meaning: finite lower and upper bounds on y

knowledge_statements.title: Envelope Dependence on Variable Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic strengthening of McCormick envelopes under bound contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B'=[l_x',u_x']\times[l_y',u_y']\subseteq B=[l_x,u_x]\times[l_y,u_y]\), and let \(M(B)\) denote the McCormick relaxation of \(z=xy\) over \(B\). Then \[M(B')\subseteq M(B)\cap(B'\times\mathbb R).\] Moreover, the maximum vertical distance between either bilinear surface and its corresponding affine envelope is \((u_x-l_x)(u_y-l_y)/4\). Hence contracting either variable interval cannot weaken the envelope, and fixing either variable makes the envelope exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tighter variable bounds strengthen McCormick inequalities; envelope error scales with the product of interval widths and vanishes when either variable is fixed.
assumptions_latex: \(B'\subseteq B\) are finite rectangles
\(M(B)\) is the McCormick relaxation over \(B\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(B')\subseteq M(B)\cap(B'\times\mathbb R)\), with one-sided maximum envelope error \((u_x-l_x)(u_y-l_y)/4\)

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Factor RLT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-level RLT inequalities obtained from products of variable-bound slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given finite bounds \(l_i\le x_i\le u_i\), form the four valid products \((x_i-l_i)(x_j-l_j)\ge0\), \((x_i-l_i)(u_j-x_j)\ge0\), \((u_i-x_i)(x_j-l_j)\ge0\), and \((u_i-x_i)(u_j-x_j)\ge0\). Expand each product and replace every \(x_ix_j\) by a symmetric lifted variable \(X_{ij}\). The resulting linear inequalities are added to the lifted model; for each pair \((i,j)\), they coincide with the four McCormick inequalities for \(X_{ij}=x_ix_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bound-factor RLT multiplies nonnegative bound slacks, expands the products, and linearizes quadratic monomials to obtain McCormick inequalities in lifted space.
assumptions_latex: \(l_i\le x_i\le u_i\) with finite bounds
\(X_{ij}=X_{ji}\) represents \(x_ix_j\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Linearizing the four bound-factor products yields valid lifted inequalities for \(X_{ij}=x_ix_j\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bound-slack product construction correctly yields the pairwise McCormick inequalities after lifting, and algorithm is suitable for this construction leaf. An authoritative RLT source with a specific locator is absent.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Factor RLT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: RLT inequalities generated by multiplying a linear-constraint slack by bound slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a^\top x\le b\) and \(l_j\le x_j\le u_j\). Multiply the nonnegative slack \(b-a^\top x\) separately by \(x_j-l_j\) and \(u_j-x_j\), expand, and replace \(x_ix_j\) by \(X_{ij}\). For example, the first product gives \[bx_j-bl_j-\sum_i a_iX_{ij}+l_j\sum_i a_ix_i\ge0.\] Repeating this operation for selected constraints and variables produces valid linear inequalities in the lifted \((x,X)\)-space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint-factor RLT multiplies a linear-constraint slack by variable-bound slacks and linearizes the expanded products into valid lifted inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(a^\top x\le b\)
\(l_j\le x_j\le u_j\)
\(X_{ij}\) represents \(x_ix_j\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The linearized slack products are valid for every lifted point satisfying \(X_{ij}=x_ix_j\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed expansion of the constraint slack times the lower-bound slack is correct, and algorithm fits the generation procedure. The specialized RLT construction has no inspectable source locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected RLT Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Original-space inequalities obtained by projecting an RLT lifted relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_{\mathrm{RLT}}=\{(x,X):A x+B\,\operatorname{vec}(X)\le d\}\) be an RLT relaxation, and define its projection \(P_x=\{x:\exists X\text{ with }(x,X)\in P_{\mathrm{RLT}}\}\). Any inequality \(\alpha^\top x\le\beta\) valid for \(P_x\), obtained by eliminating \(X\) or by a nonnegative linear combination of lifted inequalities whose \(X\)-coefficients cancel, is a projected RLT cut. It is valid for every original feasible point represented in \(P_{\mathrm{RLT}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected RLT cut eliminates lifted product variables from valid RLT inequalities, producing an original-space inequality valid for all represented feasible points.
assumptions_latex: \(P_{\mathrm{RLT}}\) contains every exact lift of an original feasible point
\(P_x\) is the projection of \(P_{\mathrm{RLT}}\) onto \(x\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every inequality valid for \(P_x\) is valid for the original feasible set

notation.meaning: projection of the RLT relaxation onto original variables

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection-validity statement is mathematically sound, but no authoritative projected-RLT source is cited. The record primarily defines and characterizes a cut-generation/projection procedure, so algorithm or definition would fit this terminal container better than representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Order RLT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree-indexed RLT construction using products of multiple constraint and bound factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an order \(r\ge1\). Form products of at most \(r\) nonnegative bound or constraint slacks, multiply eligible original polynomial constraints by products whose total degree remains within the chosen order, expand, and replace each monomial \(\prod_{i\in S}x_i\) by a lifted variable \(y_S\). Impose consistent linearizations for repeated monomials and retain all lower-order inequalities. The order-\(r+1\) relaxation therefore contains every order-\(r\) constraint, so its projection is no weaker than the order-\(r\) projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Higher-order RLT multiplies more nonnegative factors and lifts higher-degree monomials, producing a nested sequence of increasingly strong linear relaxations.
assumptions_latex: All multiplied factors are nonnegative on the original feasible set
A consistent lifted variable is used for each monomial
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projected order-\(r+1\) relaxation is contained in the projected order-\(r\) relaxation

notation.meaning: lifted variable for the monomial indexed by S

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits a hierarchy-construction leaf, but the meaning of order r, eligible multipliers, degree truncation, and retained consistency constraints varies across RLT conventions. Without a specific authoritative source, the asserted nesting cannot be reliably matched to one precise hierarchy.

knowledge_statements.title: Shor Semidefinite Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard matrix-lifting relaxation for a quadratically constrained quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(x^\top Q_0x+q_0^\top x+c_0\) subject to \(x^\top Q_kx+q_k^\top x+c_k\le0\) for \(k=1,\ldots,m\). Introduce \(X\in\mathbb S^n\), replace each \(x^\top Q_kx\) by \(Q_k\mathbin{\bullet}X\), and impose \[\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\] Dropping the exact rank-one condition \(X=xx^\top\) gives the Shor semidefinite relaxation. For minimization, its optimum is a lower bound on the QCQP optimum; binary variables may additionally impose \(X_{ii}=x_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shor relaxation replaces the rank-one product matrix by a positive-semidefinite lifted matrix, yielding an SDP lower bound for a minimization QCQP.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_k\in\mathbb S^n\) for \(k=0,\ldots,m\)
The QCQP is posed as a minimization problem
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing \(X=xx^\top\) by \(\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\) yields a valid semidefinite relaxation and a lower bound

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lifted PSD relaxation and lower-bound conclusion are mathematically standard, and representation is appropriate. The cited locator addresses the SDP cone generically rather than the Shor QCQP relaxation, rank-one lifting, or binary diagonal equations, so a Shor-specific section, theorem, or page locator is required.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) represent a lifted quadratic point.
The intended semidefinite constraint is \(Y(x,X):=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y(x,X)\succeq0\Longrightarrow X_{ii}\ge x_i^2\) and \(X_{ii}X_{jj}\ge X_{ij}^2\) for all selected pairs \(i<j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise conic outer approximation of the Shor lifted positive-semidefinite constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Y(x,X):=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\), replace \(Y(x,X)\succeq0\) by positive-semidefiniteness of selected \(2\times2\) principal submatrices. The minors indexed by \(\{0,i\}\) give \(X_{ii}\ge x_i^2\), equivalently \(\|(2x_i,X_{ii}-1)\|_2\le X_{ii}+1\). Minors indexed by \(\{i,j\}\) give \(X_{ii},X_{jj}\ge0\) and \(X_{ij}^2\le X_{ii}X_{jj}\), equivalently \(\|(2X_{ij},X_{ii}-X_{jj})\|_2\le X_{ii}+X_{jj}\). These second-order-cone constraints are necessary for the lifted semidefinite constraint and therefore define an outer relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enforcing selected two-by-two positive-semidefinite minors of the lifted moment matrix yields second-order-cone constraints and an outer approximation of the full semidefinite relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order-Cone Relaxations

assumptions_latex: \(Y\in\mathbb S^m\).
\(\mathcal I\subseteq2^{\{1,\ldots,m\}}\) is a prescribed family of index sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y\succeq0\Longrightarrow Y[I,I]\succeq0\) for every \(I\in\mathcal I\), while the converse requires sufficiently complete minor coverage.

notation.meaning: principal submatrix indexed by the set I
selected family of principal index sets

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selected principal-submatrix formulation of a partial semidefinite relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(Y\in\mathbb S^m\) and an index family \(\mathcal I\), the principal-minor relaxation of \(Y\succeq0\) is \(Y[I,I]\succeq0\) for every \(I\in\mathcal I\). Equivalently, every principal minor of each selected submatrix is nonnegative. If \(\mathcal I\) contains only sets of cardinality at most \(k<m\), the resulting feasible set contains \(\mathbb S_+^m\). It equals \(\mathbb S_+^m\) when the imposed conditions include all principal minors, but selected lower-order minors generally yield a strict outer approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A principal-minor relaxation requires selected principal submatrices to be positive semidefinite; incomplete or bounded-order selections generally provide only an outer approximation of the PSD cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Principal-Minor Relaxations

children.title: Partial-PSD Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Positive-semidefinite restrictions imposed on selected portions of a lifted matrix.

assumptions_latex: \(Y\in\mathbb S^m\).
\(\mathcal C\) is a family of subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb S_+^m\subseteq\{Y:Y[C,C]\succeq0\ \forall C\in\mathcal C\}\), with equality when \(\mathcal C\) contains the full index set.

notation.meaning: family of index blocks on which PSD is enforced

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise positive-semidefinite outer approximation of one lifted matrix constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an index-block family \(\mathcal C\), define the partial-PSD cone by \(\mathcal K_{\mathcal C}:=\{Y\in\mathbb S^m:Y[C,C]\succeq0\text{ for every }C\in\mathcal C\}\). It is a closed convex cone containing \(\mathbb S_+^m\). Enlarging any block or adding a block can only shrink \(\mathcal K_{\mathcal C}\). If \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\in\mathcal C\), then \(\mathcal K_{\mathcal C}=\mathbb S_+^m\); otherwise equality is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial-PSD relaxation enforces positive semidefiniteness only on selected principal blocks. It is convex, contains the full PSD cone, and tightens as blocks are added or enlarged.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial-PSD Relaxations

children.title: Minor Selection Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural criteria governing which matrix subsets receive semidefinite enforcement.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C_1\) and \(\mathcal C_2\) are families of index blocks for matrices in \(\mathbb S^m\).
For every \(C\in\mathcal C_1\), some \(D\in\mathcal C_2\) satisfies \(C\subseteq D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal K_{\mathcal C_2}\subseteq\mathcal K_{\mathcal C_1}\).

notation.meaning: partial-PSD cone induced by a block family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance order for static or adaptive families of selected principal blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal K_{\mathcal C}:=\{Y:Y[C,C]\succeq0\text{ for all }C\in\mathcal C\}\). If every block selected by \(\mathcal C_1\) is contained in a block selected by \(\mathcal C_2\), then \(\mathcal K_{\mathcal C_2}\subseteq\mathcal K_{\mathcal C_1}\). Thus all-pairs selection dominates diagonal-only selection, bounded-order selection tightens monotonically with the order, and an adaptive regime remains valid when it adds blocks violated by the current relaxation point. Computational cost, however, increases with the number and sizes of the selected semidefinite blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A selection regime dominates another when its blocks cover the other's blocks. Larger, more numerous, or adaptively violated blocks give tighter partial-PSD relaxations at greater computational cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Minor Selection Regimes

children.title: Partial-PSD Coverage Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Interaction patterns left uncontrolled by incomplete semidefinite coverage.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C\) contains only proper subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local conditions \(Y[C,C]\succeq0\) need not imply \(Y\succeq0\); for \(m=3\), \(Y(\rho)\) with \(-1<\rho<-1/2\) is an explicit witness.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit boundary showing that local PSD coverage may miss a global negative eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m=3\), let \(Y(\rho):=(1-\rho)I_3+\rho\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\). Every \(1\times1\) and \(2\times2\) principal submatrix is positive semidefinite whenever \(|\rho|\le1\). The eigenvalues of \(Y(\rho)\) are \(1-\rho\), with multiplicity two, and \(1+2ho\). Hence, for \(-1<\rho<-1/2\), all proper principal submatrices are positive semidefinite but \(Y(\rho)\not\succeq0\). Therefore coverage by all blocks of order at most two does not recover the full PSD cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even all pairwise PSD constraints can miss global indefiniteness: a three-dimensional equicorrelation matrix with correlation below minus one-half has PSD pairs but a negative global eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial-PSD Coverage Boundaries

children.title: Projected SDP Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cuts obtained by projecting lifted semidefinite restrictions into a lower-dimensional space.

assumptions_latex: \(Y\in\mathbb S^m\) is intended to satisfy \(Y\succeq0\).
\(P\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y\succeq0\Longrightarrow P^\top YP\succeq0\), and any \(v\) with \(v^\top P^\top YPv<0\) yields the violated valid cut \(\langle Y,Pvv^\top P^\top\rangle\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear separation certificate obtained from a negative direction in a projected matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(P\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\), the constraint \(Y\succeq0\) implies \(P^\top YP\succeq0\). If a relaxation point \(\bar Y\) violates this projected constraint, choose \(v\in\mathbb R^r\) with \(v^\top P^\top\bar YPv<0\). Then \(\langle Y,Pvv^\top P^\top\rangle\ge0\) is valid for every \(Y\succeq0\) and is violated by \(\bar Y\). The pair \((P,v)\) is therefore a directly checkable separation certificate without imposing the full semidefinite constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative eigenvector of a projected lifted matrix produces a valid linear inequality separating the current point from the PSD cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Projected SDP Cuts

children.title: Spectral Cuts
children.top_down_role: Separating inequalities derived from violated eigenstructure.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-one linear PSD cut generated by a negative spectral direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\ge2\) and let \(\bar Y u=\lambda u\), where \(\bar Y\in\mathbb S^m\), \(u\in\mathbb R^m\), \(\|u\|_2=1\), and \(\lambda<0\). Every \(Y\succeq0\) satisfies the spectral inequality \(u^\top Yu=\langle uu^\top,Y\rangle\ge0\), whereas \(u^\top\bar Yu=\lambda<0\). Thus the rank-one matrix \(uu^\top\succeq0\) certifies a valid separating cut. Adding cuts for one or more negative eigenvectors removes the detected indefinite directions, but finitely many selected directions need not enforce \(Y\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In dimension at least two, each negative eigenvector of the current lifted matrix defines a violated rank-one linear inequality valid for every positive-semidefinite matrix; finitely many selected directions need not characterize the full PSD cone.
assumptions_latex: \(m\ge2\) and \(\bar Y\in\mathbb S^m\) is a relaxation point.
\(u\in\mathbb R^m\) is a unit eigenvector of \(\bar Y\) with eigenvalue \(\lambda<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(u^\top Yu=\langle uu^\top,Y\rangle\ge0\) is valid for \(Y\succeq0\) and violated by \(\bar Y\); finitely many selected directional cuts need not characterize \(\mathbb S_+^m\).

children.title: Projection Strength Regimes
children.top_down_role: Conditions controlling how much semidefinite strength survives projection.

assumptions_latex: \(P_1\in\mathbb R^{m\times r_1}\) and \(P_2\in\mathbb R^{m\times r_2}\).
\(\operatorname{range}(P_1)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(P_2)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_2^\top YP_2\succeq0\Longrightarrow P_1^\top YP_1\succeq0\); if \(P_2\) has full row rank, its projected constraint is equivalent to \(Y\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: column space of a projection matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance and exactness regimes determined by inclusion of projected subspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\operatorname{range}(P_1)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(P_2)\), then \(P_1=P_2R\) for some matrix \(R\), so \(P_2^\top YP_2\succeq0\) implies \(P_1^\top YP_1=R^\top(P_2^\top YP_2)R\succeq0\). Hence the larger projected subspace gives the stronger relaxation. When \(P\) has full row rank, every \(u\in\mathbb R^m\) equals \(Pv\) for some \(v\), and \(P^\top YP\succeq0\) is equivalent to \(Y\succeq0\). Proper subspaces can leave negative directions undetected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected PSD constraints strengthen as their subspaces grow. A full-space projection recovers the complete PSD condition, while proper subspaces may miss negative directions.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Strength Regimes

children.title: Perspective Convexification Principle
children.top_down_role: Convexification families for indicator-controlled convex quadratic terms.

assumptions_latex: \(t_i\) is an epigraph variable for \(q_i x_i^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(S_i)=\{(x_i,z_i,t_i):0\le z_i\le1,\ t_i\ge q_i x_i^2/z_i\}\) under the closed-perspective convention.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: closed perspective hull of a scalar on-off convex quadratic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed convex hull of an unbounded scalar on-off quadratic epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(S_i:=\{(x_i,z_i,t_i):z_i\in\{0,1\},\ x_i=0\text{ if }z_i=0,\ t_i\ge q_i x_i^2\}\), where \(q_i>0\). Its closed convex hull is \(\{(x_i,z_i,t_i):0\le z_i\le1,\ t_i\ge q_i x_i^2/z_i\}\), using the closed-perspective convention that \(x_i^2/z_i=0\) at \((x_i,z_i)=(0,0)\) and is \(+\infty\) when \(z_i=0\) and \(x_i\ne0\). For a separable sum, intersecting these coordinatewise hulls gives the product epigraph formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed hull of a scalar on-off quadratic epigraph replaces the quadratic by its perspective, with value zero only at the inactive origin.
knowledge_statements.title: Separable Perspective Hulls

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar closed-perspective hull is mathematically standard and the representation kind fits, but no inspectable citation is supplied for the exact hull claim.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(tz\ge qx^2\) is a rotated-second-order-cone representation of \(t\ge qx^2/z\) with the closed-perspective convention.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: rotated-cone representation of a scalar quadratic perspective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rotated-cone formulation of the scalar quadratic perspective relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q>0\), the closed perspective epigraph \(t\ge qx^2/z\), \(0\le z\le1\), is represented by \(t\ge0\), \(z\ge0\), and \(tz\ge qx^2\). Equivalently, it is the rotated-second-order-cone constraint \(\|(2\sqrt q\,x,t-z)\|_2\le t+z\). At \(z=0\), these conditions force \(x=0\); at \(z>0\), division by \(z\) recovers the perspective inequality. Replacing binary activation by \(0\le z\le1\) therefore gives a convex conic relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar quadratic perspective is exactly representable by a rotated second-order cone, which also forces the continuous variable to vanish when activation is zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Conic Perspective Relaxations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rotated-cone representation is correct and fits the conic-relaxation leaf, but the record supplies no source with a specific locator.

assumptions_latex: \(q>0\), \(0\le z\le1\), and \(t\in\mathbb R\).
The closed perspective is \(\phi(x,z)=qx^2/z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge2q\alpha x-q\alpha^2z\) for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\) is equivalent to \(t\ge\phi(x,z)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: supporting-hyperplane representation of a scalar quadratic perspective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite linear-cut representation and finite outer approximation of a scalar perspective epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), the inequality \(t\ge2q\alpha x-q\alpha^2z\) is valid for the closed epigraph of \(\phi(x,z):=qx^2/z\). Moreover, \(\phi(x,z)=\sup_{\alpha\in\mathbb R}\{2q\alpha x-q\alpha^2z\}\) for \(z\ge0\), under the closed-perspective convention. Consequently, imposing all such inequalities exactly represents \(t\ge\phi(x,z)\), while imposing a finite parameter set \(A\subset\mathbb R\) gives the polyhedral relaxation \(t\ge2q\alpha x-q\alpha^2z\) for every \(\alpha\in A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic perspective equals the supremum of its linear perspective cuts. All cuts give the exact epigraph; any finite subset gives a polyhedral outer relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Perspective-Cut Relaxations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The supremum formula and finite-cut outer relaxation are correct, but the exact perspective-cut representation lacks an inspectable authoritative citation.

assumptions_latex: \(z_i\in\{0,1\}\) and \(x_i=0\) whenever \(z_i=0\).
The quadratic form may contain cross terms between variables with distinct indicators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Separate scalar perspectives are not generally an exact or valid hull description for a coupled quadratic unless the quadratic admits an indicator-compatible separable decomposition.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: cross-term cancellation obstructs coordinatewise perspective convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cross-term cancellation marks the boundary of exact coordinatewise perspective convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(Q=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\), so \(x^\top Qx=(x_1+x_2)^2\), with separate indicators \(z_1,z_2\) and constraints \(x_i=0\) when \(z_i=0\). The integer point \((z_1,z_2,x_1,x_2,t)=(1,1,1,-1,0)\) is feasible. Any rule that independently perspectives the diagonal terms would require \(t\ge x_1^2/z_1+x_2^2/z_2=2\) there, so it is not even valid for this coupled epigraph. Exact coordinatewise perspectives therefore require a separable, indicator-compatible decomposition; cross-term cancellation falls outside that regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent perspectives can fail for coupled quadratics: cross terms may cancel diagonal costs, so separately perspectivizing those diagonals can exclude feasible integer points.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonseparable Perspective Limits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed cancellation counterexample is valid and fits the failure-boundary leaf, but the broader claim that exact coordinatewise perspectives require an indicator-compatible separable decomposition needs authoritative sourcing and careful qualification.

children.title: Disjunctive Quadratic Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Quadratic-specific relaxations generated from integrality and spatial disjunctions.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Old Wine in a New Bottle: The MILP Road to MIQCP
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Old Wine in a New Bottle: The MILP Road to MIQCP

assumptions_latex: The lifted relaxation uses variables \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(X\in\mathbb{S}^n\), with \(X_{ij}\) representing \(x_i x_j\).
The selected variable satisfies \(x_k\in\{0,1\}\) in the original mixed-integer model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha+\beta^\top x+\langle C,X\rangle\ge 0\) is valid for the original lifted feasible set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines cuts obtained from one binary-variable disjunction in a quadratic lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{S}^n\) be a lifted relaxation and let \(k\) index a binary variable. Define the integrality-disjunctive set by \[D_k=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}\bigl((R\cap\{x_k=0\})\cup(R\cap\{x_k=1\})\bigr).\] An integrality-disjunction quadratic cut is any affine inequality \[\alpha+\beta^\top x+\langle C,X\rangle\ge0\] valid for \(D_k\). Under the substitution \(X=xx^\top\), the inequality becomes the quadratic inequality \(\alpha+\beta^\top x+x^\top Cx\ge0\), and validity for \(D_k\) implies validity for every original feasible point satisfying \(x_k\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic cut is obtained by convexifying the two lifted branches of a binary-variable disjunction and taking any affine inequality valid for that hull.
knowledge_statements.title: Integrality-Disjunction Quadratic Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the cut-family container, but no source or inspectable locator supports this specialized disjunctive-cut terminology and construction.

knowledge_statements.title: Spatial-Disjunction Quadratic Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines quadratic cuts derived from strengthened local lifted relaxations on the two sides of a spatial split.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{S}^n\) be the original lifted feasible set, let \(R\) be a convex relaxation of \(F\), and let \(\tau\) lie strictly between the current bounds of \(x_k\). Let \(R^-\subseteq R\) and \(R^+\subseteq R\) be convex localized relaxations satisfying \[F\cap\{x_k\le\tau\}\subseteq R^-\quad\text{and}\quad F\cap\{x_k\ge\tau\}\subseteq R^+.\] Define \[D_{k,\tau}=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(R^-\cup R^+).\] A spatial-disjunction quadratic cut is an affine inequality \[\alpha+\beta^\top x+\langle C,X\rangle\ge0\] valid for \(D_{k,\tau}\). It is valid for \(F\), and under \(X=xx^\top\) it becomes \[\alpha+\beta^\top x+x^\top Cx\ge0.\] If \(D_{k,\tau}\subsetneq R\), such an inequality may separate points of \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spatial-disjunction quadratic cut is valid for the convex hull of two strengthened local lifted relaxations associated with the two sides of a coordinate split.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{S}^n\), and \(R\) is convex.
The split point \(\tau\) lies strictly between the current bounds of \(x_k\).
The localized convex relaxations \(R^-\) and \(R^+\) contain the corresponding branches of \(F\) and are contained in \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha+\beta^\top x+\langle C,X\rangle\ge0\) is valid for \(F\), and it can strengthen \(R\) when \(D_{k,\tau}\subsetneq R\).

notation.meaning: Localized lifted relaxations on the two sides of the split.
Closed convex hull of the localized branch relaxations.

children.title: Lifted Disjunctive Quadratic Sets
children.top_down_role: Extended quadratic relaxation spaces associated with selected disjunctions.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Disjunctive Quadratic Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A perspective-based extended representation of the convex hull of finitely many compact convex branch sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_r\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{S}^n\), \(r=1,\ldots,m\), be nonempty compact convex sets, and define \[\widehat S_r=\operatorname{cl}\{(\lambda,\lambda x,\lambda X):\lambda>0,\ (x,X)\in S_r\}.\] Define \[\mathcal D=\left\{(x,X,\{x^r,X^r,\lambda_r\}_{r=1}^m):(\lambda_r,x^r,X^r)\in\widehat S_r,\ \sum_{r=1}^m\lambda_r=1,\ x=\sum_{r=1}^m x^r,\ X=\sum_{r=1}^m X^r\right\}.\] Then \[\pi_{x,X}(\mathcal D)=\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{r=1}^m S_r\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many compact convex branches, perspective-scaled branch variables give an extended representation whose projection is exactly the convex hull of their union.
assumptions_latex: Each \(S_r\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{S}^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
The disjunction has finitely many branches \(r=1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_{x,X}(\mathcal D)=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{r=1}^m S_r)\).

notation.meaning: Compact convex branch sets in lifted quadratic variables.
Projection onto the aggregate quadratic variables.

children.title: Projected Quadratic Cut Families
children.top_down_role: Quadratic cuts obtained after eliminating auxiliary lifted coordinates.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal D\) is a lifted disjunctive set in variables \((x,X,u)\).
Each stated inequality is valid for \(\mathcal D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every member of \(\mathcal C\) is valid for \(P=\pi_{x,X}(\mathcal D)\).

notation.meaning: Projection of the extended disjunctive set.
Auxiliary lifted variables eliminated by projection.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the inequalities remaining after auxiliary variables are eliminated from a lifted disjunctive formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\pi_{x,X}(\mathcal D)\). A projected quadratic cut family for \(\mathcal D\) is a collection \[\mathcal C=\{\alpha_s+\beta_s^\top x+\langle C_s,X\rangle\ge0:s\in I\}\] such that every inequality is valid for \(P\). Equivalently, each member is implied by the constraints defining \(\mathcal D\) after elimination of \(u\). When \(X=xx^\top\), member \(s\) becomes \[\alpha_s+\beta_s^\top x+x^\top C_sx\ge0.\] Thus \(\mathcal C\) is valid in the original variables, although a finite subfamily need not describe the complete projection \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected quadratic cuts are inequalities in the original lifted variables obtained after eliminating branch-specific or other auxiliary variables from an extended disjunctive set.
knowledge_statements.title: Projected Quadratic Cut Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the projected-cut container, and the mathematical distinction between the complete projection and a finite cut subfamily is sound. No citation or locator supports the specialized formulation.

children.title: Projection Loss Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where eliminating lifted coordinates weakens the retained disjunctive information.

assumptions_latex: Projection is performed separately on multiple lifted relaxations before they are combined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: In general, \(\pi(E_1\cap E_2)\subsetneq\pi(E_1)\cap\pi(E_2)\).

notation.meaning: Two extended sets sharing an eliminated variable.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separate projection can discard compatibility carried by shared auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Projection commutes with unions but need not commute with intersections. In particular, let \[E_1=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^2:y=x\},\qquad E_2=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^2:y=-x\}.\] Then \[\pi_x(E_1)=\pi_x(E_2)=\mathbb{R},\qquad \pi_x(E_1)\cap\pi_x(E_2)=\mathbb{R},\] whereas \[\pi_x(E_1\cap E_2)=\{0\}.\] Consequently, projecting lifted quadratic relaxations separately and then intersecting their projections can be strictly weaker than first intersecting the extended formulations with shared auxiliary variables and then projecting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating shared auxiliary variables before combining relaxations can lose compatibility constraints; projection of an intersection may be strictly smaller than the intersection of projections.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Loss Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly demonstrates strict failure of projection to commute with intersection and fits a failure-boundary container, but the record supplies no source or explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Localized Quadratic Relaxation Family
children.top_down_role: Localized finite-resolution relaxations for squares and products.

assumptions_latex: The variable satisfies \(x\in[\ell,u]\) with a partition \(\ell=p_0<\cdots<p_m=u\).
The lifted variable represents \(w=x^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On an active interval \([p_{r-1},p_r]\), the exact convex hull is \(x^2\le w\le(p_{r-1}+p_r)x-p_{r-1}p_r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Piecewise convexification of one square graph over a bounded interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each interval \(I_r=[p_{r-1},p_r]\), the convex hull of the restricted square graph is \[\operatorname{conv}\{(x,w):x\in I_r,\ w=x^2\}=\{(x,w):x\in I_r,\ x^2\le w\le(p_{r-1}+p_r)x-p_{r-1}p_r\}.\] A univariate-square partition relaxation selects one interval using \(z_r\in\{0,1\}\) and \(\sum_{r=1}^m z_r=1\), then enforces the corresponding hull, directly or through a disaggregated formulation. Relaxing the selectors to \([0,1]\) yields a valid convex relaxation; refining the partition cannot weaken its projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition the variable domain and impose the exact convex hull of the square graph on the selected interval; smaller intervals give tighter secant bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Univariate-Square Partitioning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The interval hull formula is correct and the representation kind fits. The selector relaxation and monotonic refinement claim depend on using a specified ideal disjunctive formulation, which is not given or sourced.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in[a,b]\) and \(y\in[c,d]\), where \(a<b\) and \(c<d\).
The lifted variable represents \(w=xy\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The four McCormick inequalities describe the convex hull of the bilinear graph on each active rectangle.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rectangle-wise McCormick convexification of a bounded bilinear graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a rectangle \([a,b]\times[c,d]\), the convex hull of \(w=xy\) is given by \[w\ge ay+cx-ac,\qquad w\ge by+dx-bd,\] \[w\le by+cx-bc,\qquad w\le ay+dx-ad.\] Bilinear rectangle partitioning divides the domains of \(x\) and \(y\) into intervals, activates one product rectangle, and imposes these four inequalities using that rectangle's endpoints. The union of the active-rectangle hulls contains the bilinear graph exactly, and its convex extended formulation projects to a valid relaxation. Refining either coordinate partition cannot enlarge the resulting projected relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition the two factor domains into rectangles and impose the four exact McCormick hull inequalities on the selected rectangle.
knowledge_statements.title: Bilinear Rectangle Partitioning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The four McCormick inequalities correctly describe the rectangle-wise bilinear hull. The projected refinement claim requires a precisely specified nested extended formulation, and no supporting citation is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiparametric Disaggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-box perspective disaggregation for interacting bounded variables and their lifted quadratic products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\) be finitely many boxes covering the bounded parameter domain, and let each \(R_r\subseteq\mathbb{R}^q\times\mathbb{S}^q\) be a nonempty compact convex lifted relaxation valid on \(B_r\). Define \[\widehat R_r=\operatorname{cl}\{(z,zx,zX):z>0,\ (x,X)\in R_r\}.\] A multiparametric disaggregation introduces \((z_r,x^r,X^r)\in\widehat R_r\) and imposes \[\sum_{r=1}^m z_r=1,\qquad x=\sum_{r=1}^m x^r,\qquad X=\sum_{r=1}^m X^r.\] Its projection onto \((x,X)\) equals \[\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{r=1}^m R_r\right).\] Requiring \(z_r\in\{0,1\}\) selects one boxwise relaxation, whereas allowing \(z_r\ge0\) gives the convex-hull formulation above.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perspective-scale box-specific variables and quadratic lifts, then aggregate them with box weights to represent the convex hull of the localized relaxations.
assumptions_latex: The bounded parameter domain is covered by finitely many boxes \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\).
Each \(R_r\) is a nonempty compact convex lifted relaxation valid on \(B_r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The continuous disaggregated formulation projects to \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{r=1}^m R_r)\).

notation.meaning: Box weights or binary box activations.
Closed perspective cone of the boxwise relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Partition Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive best-bound refinement using localized quadratic relaxations, with explicit conditions for monotone bounds and asymptotic convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be continuous on a compact feasible region contained in the initial partition. At iteration \(k\), solve the valid relaxation on every active cell \(B\in\mathcal P_k\), set \[L_k=\min_{B\in\mathcal P_k}L(B),\] and update the best feasible value \(U_k\). Stop when \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\). Otherwise refine selected globally competitive cells. Require every child \(B'\subseteq B\) to satisfy \(L(B')\ge L(B)\), require every cell that remains globally competitive to be refined indefinitely, and require \(L(B_j)\to\min\{f(x):x\in B_j\text{ is feasible}\}\) along every indefinitely refined nested sequence with \(\operatorname{diam}(B_j)\to0\). Under these conditions, \(L_k\) is nondecreasing and converges to the global optimum value \(f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refine cells that can still determine the global lower bound, using inherited monotone local bounds; exhaustive shrinking and local consistency yield convergence to the global optimum value.
assumptions_latex: The feasible region is compact and \(f\) is continuous on it.
Active cells form a finite partition, and refinement replaces a cell by finitely many subcells covering it.
Each cell relaxation gives a valid lower bound, and every child lower bound is at least its parent's lower bound.
Every cell remaining globally competitive is refined indefinitely, its nested diameters tend to zero, and the local bounds are consistent on such shrinking sequences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence \(L_k\) is nondecreasing and satisfies \(L_k\to f^*\).

notation.meaning: Valid relaxation lower bound on cell B.
Best feasible objective value found by iteration k.

children.title: Relaxation Projection-Composition Calculus
children.top_down_role: Relationships among extended relaxations, their projections, and compatible combinations.

assumptions_latex: \(E\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) is an extended relaxation in variables \((x,u)\).
\(P=\pi_x(E)\) is its exact projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Optimization of any objective depending only on \(x\) has the same value over \(E\) and \(P\).

notation.meaning: Its projection into the original variables.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares an exact extended formulation with its complete projection, not a truncated projected cut family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), \[\inf\{f(x):(x,u)\in E\}=\inf\{f(x):x\in P\}.\] Thus an extended relaxation and its exact projection have identical strength for objectives and constraints expressed only in \(x\). Differences arise from representation: \(E\) may have more variables but fewer or simpler constraints, whereas an explicit description of \(P\) may require many inequalities. If only a subfamily of valid projected inequalities is retained, defining \(P'\supseteq P\), then the resulting relaxation can be strictly weaker than \(E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended relaxation and its exact projection give identical bounds for original-variable objectives, but a partial projected description can be weaker.
knowledge_statements.title: Extended versus Projected Relaxations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact-projection equality and warning about truncated projected descriptions are mathematically sound and fit the property container, but no citation or standard-field rationale is provided.

assumptions_latex: The base polyhedron is \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_i^\top x\le b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\).
\(Y\in\mathbb{S}^n\) represents \(xx^\top\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The combined relaxation is contained in both its RLT-only and SDP-only counterparts.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intersection of first-order semidefinite lifting with linearized products of valid linear slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[M(x,Y)=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&Y\end{pmatrix}.\] For every pair \(i,j\), linearizing the valid product \((b_i-a_i^\top x)(b_j-a_j^\top x)\ge0\) gives \[b_i b_j-b_i a_j^\top x-b_j a_i^\top x+\langle a_i a_j^\top,Y\rangle\ge0.\] The RLT-SDP combination consists of the base constraints, all selected RLT inequalities, and \[M(x,Y)\succeq0.\] Hence its feasible region equals the intersection of the corresponding RLT and SDP lifted relaxations and is contained in each one separately. Additional valid linear equations linking entries of \(Y\) may be imposed without changing this containment claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combine a positive-semidefinite moment matrix with linearized products of linear-constraint slacks; the intersection dominates either relaxation used alone.
knowledge_statements.title: RLT–SDP Combinations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The RLT slack-product linearization, semidefinite moment constraint, and containment conclusion are coherent, and representation is the correct content kind. The specialized combination has no cited source or locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Perspective–Conic Combinations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed perspective hull and rotated-conic representation for an unbounded positive-semidefinite indicator quadratic epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb{S}_+^n\) with \(Q=L^\top L\), and define \[S=\{(x,t,z):z\in\{0,1\},\ z=0\Rightarrow x=0,\ t\ge x^\top Qx,\ t\ge0\}.\] Then \[\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(S)=\{(x,t,z):0\le z\le1,\ t\ge0,\ tz\ge x^\top Qx\}.\] Because \(x^\top Qx=\|Lx\|_2^2\), the inequality \(tz\ge\|Lx\|_2^2\), together with \(t,z\ge0\), is representable by a rotated second-order cone. At \(z=0\), this closed formulation forces \(Lx=0\); it forces \(x=0\) when \(Q\) is positive definite, while singular \(Q\) permits nullspace recession points introduced by closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective hull of a positive-semidefinite indicator quadratic epigraph is rotated-conic; for singular quadratic matrices, its zero-indicator face can contain nullspace recession points.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb{S}_+^n\) and \(Q=L^\top L\).
The original binary set satisfies \(z=0\Rightarrow x=0\) and has no additional bounds on \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(S)=\{(x,t,z):0\le z\le1,\ t\ge0,\ tz\ge x^\top Qx\}\), with a rotated-second-order-cone representation.

notation.meaning: Positive-semidefinite quadratic matrix and a factorization.
Nullspace responsible for recession points when Q is singular.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Strength–Size Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares projected feasible regions and explicit formulation size for minimization relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the feasible set and let \(R_i\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^{k_i}\) be two relaxations with \(F\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(R_i)\). Relaxation \(R_1\) is at least as strong as \(R_2\) when \(\operatorname{proj}_x(R_1)\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(R_2)\); consequently, minimizing the same objective over \(R_1\) gives a lower bound no smaller than that from \(R_2\). Its explicit size may be measured by its numbers of auxiliary variables and constraints. Strength and size are distinct: neither more constraints nor more auxiliary variables alone implies a stronger projected relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smaller projected feasible region gives a stronger minimization bound, but formulation size alone does not order relaxation strength.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(R_i)\) for \(i=1,2\).
The same minimization objective is used for both relaxations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(R_1)\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(R_2)\Rightarrow \inf_{R_1} f(x)\geq\inf_{R_2} f(x)\).

children.title: Native MIQP Node Relaxations

knowledge_statements.title: Native MIQP Node Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous convex-QP relaxation at a branch-and-bound node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization MIQP with objective \(\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\), linear constraints \(Ax\leq b\), bounds \(\ell\leq x\leq u\), integer index set \(I\), and \(Q\succeq0\). At node \(v\), replace integrality by \(x_I\in\mathbb R^{|I|}\) and impose the node bounds \(\ell^v\leq x\leq u^v\). The resulting native node relaxation is the convex quadratic program \[L_v=\inf\{\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x:Ax\leq b,\ \ell^v\leq x\leq u^v\}.\] If feasible and bounded, \(L_v\) is a valid lower bound for every integer-feasible descendant of \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relax integrality while retaining the convex quadratic objective and node bounds; the resulting QP value is a valid subtree lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\).
Node bounds preserve every integer-feasible descendant.
The problem is a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_v\leq f(x)\) for every integer-feasible descendant \(x\) of node \(v\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convex-QP node relaxation and subtree lower-bound claim are mathematically standard and fit the representation container, but no inspectable MIQP tree-search source is supplied.

children.title: Native MIQP Branching Policies

knowledge_statements.title: Native MIQP Branching Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable branching driven by a native convex-QP node solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node with optimal relaxation solution \(\bar x\), form \(J=\{j\in I:\bar x_j\notin\mathbb Z\}\). If \(J=\varnothing\), return \(\bar x\) for incumbent testing. Otherwise choose \(j\in J\) by a specified score, such as most-fractional, pseudocost, or strong-branching score, and create children with \(x_j\leq\lfloor\bar x_j\rfloor\) and \(x_j\geq\lceil\bar x_j\rceil\). Each child retains the original convex quadratic objective and all inherited constraints. Stop branching when the node is infeasible, its bound permits pruning, or its relaxation solution is integer-feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select a fractional integer variable from the QP solution and split its domain into exhaustive floor and ceiling branches.
assumptions_latex: A finite-valued optimal node-relaxation solution \(\bar x\) is available.
Each integer variable has a finite discrete domain over the root bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two child domains are disjoint and contain every integer-feasible point of the parent node.

notation.meaning: Fractional integer-variable indices at the node solution.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The floor-ceiling branching algorithm is coherent and exhaustive for integer points, but its MIQP-specific policy and termination context have no cited source.

children.title: Native Quadratic Presolve Support

knowledge_statements.title: Native Quadratic Presolve Support
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence-preserving reductions applied directly to convex MIQP data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a convex MIQP, repeatedly apply certified reductions: tighten variable bounds using linear and quadratic constraints; fix a variable when its certified bounds coincide; delete redundant constraints; substitute fixed variables into the quadratic objective and constraints; and remove zero rows or columns. Every reduction must either preserve the feasible integer points under the recorded substitution map or certify infeasibility. The algorithm terminates when no selected reduction changes the model and returns a reduced MIQP together with a recovery map from reduced feasible solutions to original feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tighten, fix, substitute, and remove redundant quadratic-model components while retaining a recovery map or an infeasibility certificate.
assumptions_latex: All bound deductions and redundancy tests are mathematically certified.
Substitution updates every affected linear and quadratic coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced model is infeasible exactly when certified so; otherwise its recoverable feasible solutions preserve the original objective values.
review_flags: native quadratic presolve rules need solver-independent source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the implementation-dependent reduction catalogue. Moreover, the claim that the reduced model is infeasible exactly when certified is too strong unless completeness of the selected infeasibility tests is established.

knowledge_statements.title: MISOCP Node Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous conic relaxation at a MISOCP branch-and-bound node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a minimization MISOCP have affine constraints \(A_ix+b_i\in\mathcal Q_i\), linear constraints, bounds, and integer index set \(I\), where \(\mathcal Q_i=\{(t,z):\|z\|_2\leq t\}\). At node \(v\), relax \(x_I\in\mathbb Z^{|I|}\) to \(x_I\in\mathbb R^{|I|}\) and impose inherited node bounds. Solving the resulting SOCP yields value \(L_v\). If it is feasible and bounded, \(L_v\) is no greater than the objective value of any integer-feasible descendant; conic infeasibility certifies that the node contains no feasible descendant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relax node integrality but retain second-order-cone constraints, obtaining an SOCP lower bound or conic infeasibility certificate.
assumptions_latex: Every \(\mathcal Q_i\) is a closed convex second-order cone.
Node restrictions do not exclude any point assigned to that node.
The model is minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_v\leq f(x)\) for every integer-feasible descendant \(x\) of node \(v\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The continuous SOCP relaxation gives the stated descendant lower bound and fits the representation container, but no MISOCP source is cited and the conditions under which solver-reported conic infeasibility constitutes a certificate are unspecified.

children.title: MISOCP Branching Policies

knowledge_statements.title: MISOCP Branching Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integrality branching using solutions or estimates from SOCP node relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve the node SOCP and let \(\bar x\) be an optimal solution. If some integer coordinate is fractional, choose \(j\in I\) using a declared score computed from fractionality, pseudocosts, or trial SOCP solves. Create children by adding \(x_j\leq\lfloor\bar x_j\rfloor\) and \(x_j\geq\lceil\bar x_j\rceil\), respectively, while retaining every conic constraint. Warm starts or approximate scores may guide selection, but pruning requires a certified bound or infeasibility conclusion. If no integer coordinate is fractional, submit \(\bar x\) for feasibility and incumbent testing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch on a fractional integer coordinate of the SOCP solution while preserving the cone system and using only certified bounds for pruning.
assumptions_latex: The node SOCP has an optimal solution \(\bar x\).
The selected coordinate \(j\) is integer-constrained and fractional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The child disjunction covers all integer-feasible points of the parent node.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The branching disjunction is mathematically valid and the algorithm kind fits, but the MISOCP-specific scoring, pruning, and certification statements lack an authoritative source.
