knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Aware Search Support
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pruning certificates derived from conic primal-dual node solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a conic node relaxation in standard form \(\inf\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\), a vector \(y\) satisfying \(c-A^\top y\in K^*\) is dual feasible and certifies the lower bound \(b^\top y\). Thus a minimization node may be pruned by bound when \(b^\top y\) is no smaller than the incumbent value. A valid conic infeasibility certificate may instead prune the node as empty. Residual-based approximate solver outputs support search decisions only after their feasibility and bound claims have been converted into certified inequalities at the required tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual-cone feasible vectors certify node lower bounds; valid conic infeasibility certificates establish empty nodes and permit safe pruning.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone and \(K^*\) is its dual cone.
The displayed dual feasibility relation is verified exactly or within a certified tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c^\top x\geq b^\top y\) for every primal-feasible \(x\).

notation.meaning: Dual cone of the primal cone.

review_flags: conic duality and certified-tolerance source required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed dual-feasibility relation correctly certifies the lower bound under the stated cone convention, and certificate is the appropriate kind. Sources are required for the unspecified infeasibility certificate and certified-tolerance claims.

children.title: Convex Quadratic Branching

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Quadratic Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustive integer-variable branching within convex quadratic branch-and-cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(v\), solve the current convex quadratic relaxation and select an integer-constrained coordinate \(j\) with fractional value \(\bar x_j\). Replace the node by two children whose additional constraints are \(x_j\leq\lfloor\bar x_j\rfloor\) and \(x_j\geq\lceil\bar x_j\rceil\). Inherited quadratic constraints and all globally valid cuts remain active in both children; locally valid cuts are inherited only when their validity regions contain the child. The split is exhaustive for integer \(x_j\), and repeated branching over finite integer domains eventually produces integer assignments unless nodes are pruned earlier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split a fractional integer coordinate into floor and ceiling children, retaining exactly those quadratic constraints and cuts valid for each child.
assumptions_latex: The selected \(j\) is integer-constrained and \(\bar x_j\notin\mathbb Z\).
Integer-variable root domains are finite.
Each inherited cut is valid on the receiving child.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every integer-feasible parent solution belongs to exactly one of the two children.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exhaustive floor-ceiling split and validity-qualified cut inheritance fit convex quadratic branch-and-cut, but no source supports the full algorithmic statement or finite-domain termination claim.

children.title: Convex Quadratic Cut Separation
children.top_down_role: Dynamic separation of valid inequalities for convex quadratic node relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Quadratic Cut Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order separation of violated convex quadratic epigraph constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+a^\top x+\beta\) with \(Q\succeq0\), and consider the epigraph constraint \(q(x)\leq t\). At a candidate \((\bar x,\bar t)\) with \(q(\bar x)>\bar t\), compute \(g=Q\bar x+a\) and add \[q(\bar x)+g^\top(x-\bar x)\leq t.\] Convexity makes this inequality valid for every epigraph-feasible point, while substitution of \((\bar x,\bar t)\) violates it. Separation may be repeated until no violation exceeds the prescribed tolerance or another node-processing limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a violated point, add the supporting tangent of the convex quadratic; it is globally valid and excludes that point.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\).
The candidate satisfies \(q(\bar x)>\bar t\) beyond the separation tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(\bar x)+\nabla q(\bar x)^\top(x-\bar x)\leq t\) is valid and separates \((\bar x,\bar t)\).

notation.meaning: Gradient of the quadratic at the candidate point.

children.title: Cut-Enhanced Quadratic Node Processing
children.top_down_role: Integration of separated cuts into repeated convex quadratic node solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Enhanced Quadratic Node Processing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative relaxation, separation, bounding, and pruning at one branch-and-cut node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the node relaxation with inherited bounds, convex quadratic constraints, and valid inherited cuts. Solve it; if infeasible, prune. Otherwise obtain \((\bar x,L_v)\), separate every enabled cut family at \(\bar x\), add cuts whose violation exceeds tolerance, and re-solve. Repeat until no qualifying cut is found or a prescribed round limit is reached. Then prune if \(L_v\) meets the incumbent cutoff, accept for incumbent testing if all integrality and original constraints hold, or branch otherwise. Only certified relaxation bounds may justify pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve and separate valid cuts, then prune by certified bounds, test an integer solution, or branch.
assumptions_latex: Every generated cut is valid for the node's integer-feasible set.
The node relaxation is solved sufficiently accurately to certify pruning decisions.
A finite cut-round or convergence stopping rule is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure neither removes a feasible incumbent candidate by invalid cutting nor prunes a node without a valid bound or infeasibility certificate.
review_flags: complete convex quadratic branch-and-cut reference required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The node-processing loop is coherent and appropriately classified as an algorithm, but no source supports the combined separation, certification, pruning, incumbent-testing, and branching procedure.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Tangent Outer Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear outer approximation of convex quadratic epigraphs and sublevel constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each convex quadratic \(q_r\), maintain sampled points \(S_r\). Replace an epigraph constraint \(q_r(x)\leq t_r\) by \(q_r(s)+\nabla q_r(s)^\top(x-s)\leq t_r\) for every \(s\in S_r\); replace \(q_r(x)\leq0\) analogously. Solve the resulting mixed-integer linear master. At its candidate \(\bar x\), evaluate the original quadratics and add the tangent at \(\bar x\) for each violated constraint. Stop when the candidate satisfies all original quadratic constraints within tolerance, the master is infeasible, or a declared iteration limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a linear master of quadratic tangents and add new tangents at candidates violating the original convex quadratics.
assumptions_latex: Every \(q_r\) is differentiable and convex.
Master integrality restrictions match those of the original model.
Violation and termination tolerances are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every tangent is a valid relaxation inequality, and termination at a feasible master candidate returns a feasible point of the original quadratic constraints.

notation.meaning: Points at which tangents for quadratic function \(q_r\) are stored.

knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient Conic Outer Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-cone separation of affine conic constraints in a mixed-integer master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider affine conic constraints \(F_r(x)=A_rx+b_r\in K_r\), where each \(K_r\) is a closed convex cone. Maintain multipliers \(Y_r\subseteq K_r^*\) and impose the linear master inequalities \(\langle y,F_r(x)\rangle\geq0\) for \(y\in Y_r\). Solve the mixed-integer master. If a candidate \(\bar x\) violates \(F_r(\bar x)\in K_r\), obtain a separating \(y\in K_r^*\) satisfying \(\langle y,F_r(\bar x)\rangle<0\), add it to \(Y_r\), and repeat. Return a candidate only after every conic membership test passes within the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent cone membership by accumulated dual-cone inequalities and add a separating multiplier whenever a master candidate violates a cone.
assumptions_latex: Each \(K_r\) is a closed convex cone.
A separation oracle returns a valid \(y\in K_r^*\) for every tested violation.
The master preserves the original integrality restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each added inequality is valid for \(F_r(x)\in K_r\) and excludes the candidate that generated it.

notation.meaning: Affine map defining a conic constraint.

review_flags: conic sign convention should be checked against source

knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Formulation Outer Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear outer approximation of an exact lifted formulation for convex quadratic constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q=(x,z)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) and \(K=\{q:F_j(q)\le 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), where each \(F_j:\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\to\mathbb{R}\) is finite, closed, and convex, and the projection of \(K\) onto \(x\) is the original continuous feasible set. For a finite set \(T\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\), choose \(g_{j,t}\in\partial F_j(t)\) and define \(H_T\) by \(F_j(t)+g_{j,t}^{\mathsf T}(q-t)\le 0\) for every \(j\) and \(t\in T\). Then \(K\subseteq H_T\), so the projection of \(H_T\), together with the original integrality restrictions, is a valid MILP outer approximation. Moreover, intersecting these inequalities over all \(t\in\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) and all \(j\) recovers \(K\), and its projection recovers the original continuous feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Supporting inequalities for convex constraints in an exact lifted space give valid finite MILP outer approximations; using them throughout the lifted domain recovers the lifted set and its original-variable projection exactly.
assumptions_latex: The lifted set is an exact formulation of the original continuous quadratic constraints.
Each defining function \(F_j:\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\to\mathbb{R}\) is finite, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every finite family of lifted supporting inequalities gives a valid outer approximation, and the family indexed by the full lifted domain recovers the exact lifted feasible set.

notation.meaning: Combined original and lifted decision vector
Exact closed convex lifted feasible set
Polyhedron defined by a finite family of supporting inequalities

children.top_down_role: Quadratic subproblem interfaces to decomposition frameworks owned elsewhere.

assumptions_latex: For every fixed master vector \(y\), the continuous quadratic subproblem is convex and satisfies strong duality whenever feasible.
The master domain for \(y\) contains all required integrality restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual optimal solutions or infeasibility rays produce valid Benders cuts in \(y\), and the accumulated master gives a lower-bounding decomposition.

notation.meaning: Value of the convex quadratic subproblem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical Benders decomposition with a convex quadratic continuous subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(y^k\in Y\), solve \(v(y^k)=\inf\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge b-By,\ x\in X\}\) with \(Q\succeq0\). If the subproblem is feasible, obtain a dual optimal solution \(\lambda^k\) and add the optimality cut \(\theta\ge\alpha(\lambda^k)+(\lambda^k)^{\mathsf T}By\), where \(\alpha(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax)\}\). If it is infeasible, add a valid feasibility cut from a dual ray. Reoptimize the master over \((y,\theta)\), and stop when its lower bound and the best feasible objective differ by at most the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a convex quadratic subproblem at each master point and use dual solutions or rays to add Benders optimality or feasibility cuts.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Benders Subproblems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No evidence is supplied, and the displayed optimality cut has the wrong dependence on y under the stated constraint and definition of alpha: the dual bound is alpha(lambda) minus lambda^T B y, not plus it. An exact quadratic-Benders source and a corrected formulation are required.

assumptions_latex: The primal quadratic objective is convex, with \(Q\succeq0\).
The relaxed coupling constraints are affine, and the remaining set \(X\) is closed and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every nonnegative multiplier, the Lagrangian quadratic subproblem supplies a valid dual lower bound; maximizing these bounds gives the Lagrangian dual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex quadratic subproblem obtained by dualizing affine coupling inequalities.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the problem \(p^*=\inf\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ x\in X\}\), define \(L(x,\lambda)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)\) and \(q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda)\). For each \(\lambda\ge0\), computing \(q(\lambda)\) is a convex quadratic subproblem and weak duality gives \(q(\lambda)\le p^*\). Hence the Lagrangian dual is \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}q(\lambda)\le p^*\). If a convex constraint qualification such as Slater's condition holds and \(p^*\) is finite, then \(d^*=p^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing affine coupling constraints creates convex quadratic subproblems whose values are lower bounds; under a constraint qualification, their best bound equals the primal optimum.

After fixing or dualizing coupling terms, the quadratic objective contains no cross-block products.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the resulting subproblem is \(\inf_{x\in X}\sum_{b=1}^B f_b(x_b)\), where \(X=\prod_{b=1}^B X_b\) and \(f_b(x_b)=\tfrac12x_b^{\mathsf T}Q_bx_b+c_b^{\mathsf T}x_b\) with \(Q_b\succeq0\). knowledge_statements.title: Spatial Node Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: McCormick-based continuous convex relaxation at a bounded spatial branch-and-bound node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node with \((x,y)\in D=[\ell_x,u_x]\times[\ell_y,u_y]\), replace \(w=xy\) by \(w\ge\ell_xy+\ell_yx-\ell_x\ell_y\), \(w\ge u_xy+u_yx-u_xu_y\), \(w\le u_xy+\ell_yx-u_x\ell_y\), and \(w\le\ell_xy+u_yx-\ell_xu_y\). These inequalities describe the convex hull of \(\{(x,y,w):(x,y)\in D,\ w=xy\}\). Applying them to every lifted bilinear term, retaining the node's other convex constraints, and relaxing all integrality restrictions produces a convex relaxation containing every original node-feasible point. For minimization, its optimal value is therefore a valid node lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a bounded search node, replace each bilinear equality by its four McCormick inequalities and relax integrality to obtain a valid continuous convex relaxation and minimization lower bound.
assumptions_latex: Every factor participating in a lifted bilinear term has finite node bounds.
All remaining constraints retained in the continuous node relaxation are convex.
Integrality restrictions are relaxed when forming the convex node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The McCormick replacements yield a continuous convex superset of the original node-feasible set and hence a valid minimization lower bound.

assumptions_latex: Both factors of each partitioned bilinear term have finite bounds.
The selected subintervals form a finite cover with pairwise disjoint interiors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The disjunctive union remains an exact representation of the bounded bilinear graph, while its piecewise convex relaxation is at least as strong as the unpartitioned envelope.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite rectangular partitioning of a bounded bilinear graph.

source_refs.locator: 2.4.2 Convergence of Multivariate Rectangular Partition Methods p. 97

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \([\ell_x,u_x]=\bigcup_{r=1}^R I_r\) and \([\ell_y,u_y]=\bigcup_{s=1}^S J_s\). Then the bounded bilinear graph satisfies \[\{(x,y,w):w=xy\}=\bigcup_{r=1}^R\bigcup_{s=1}^S\{(x,y,w):(x,y)\in I_r\times J_s,\ w=xy\}.\] Replacing each disjunct's graph by its four rectangular convex-hull inequalities and enforcing selection of one active rectangle gives a valid piecewise-convex relaxation. Because every rectangle lies inside the original box, its projection is contained in the unpartitioned McCormick relaxation, and adding partition breakpoints cannot weaken the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partitioning a bilinear domain into rectangles and imposing each rectangle's envelope yields a valid piecewise relaxation that dominates the single-box envelope.

children.top_down_role: Spatial or discrete subdivision selected directly on model variables.

assumptions_latex: The chosen variable has a nondegenerate bounded interval \([\ell_i,u_i]\).
A split point \(s\) satisfies \(\ell_i<s<u_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two children cover the parent domain exactly and have disjoint interiors, so spatial branching preserves all feasible solutions while tightening local product envelopes.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Convergence of Branch-and-Bound Type Methods p. 35

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a parent node domain \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(x_i\in[\ell_i,u_i]\), select \(s\in(\ell_i,u_i)\) and create \(D^- =D\cap\{x:x_i\le s\}\) and \(D^+=D\cap\{x:x_i\ge s\}\). Recompute every relaxation coefficient depending on the bounds of \(x_i\), then solve or queue both child relaxations. The identities \(D=D^-\cup D^+\) and \(\operatorname{int}(D^-)\cap\operatorname{int}(D^+)=\varnothing\) ensure exhaustive branching. A child is pruned when infeasible or when its valid lower bound cannot improve the incumbent objective within the stopping tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split one bounded variable at an interior point, rebuild affected relaxations in both children, and prune children using infeasibility or incumbent-based bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable Branching

children.title: Expression Branching
children.top_down_role: Subdivision selected on lifted products or composite quadratic expressions.

assumptions_latex: A nonconvex expression \(g(x)\) has computable finite bounds \([L,U]\) on the current node.
An interior threshold \(s\in(L,U)\) is selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Branching on the expression's range covers the parent feasible set and can tighten several linked nonlinear terms simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spatial disjunction imposed on a bounded nonlinear expression rather than one variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node with feasible region \(D\), choose a bounded expression \(g:D\to[L,U]\) and \(s\in(L,U)\). Form the children \(D^- =D\cap\{x:g(x)\le s\}\) and \(D^+=D\cap\{x:g(x)\ge s\}\). Introduce or retain an auxiliary variable for \(g(x)\), impose the corresponding bound in each child, and rebuild all relaxations involving that auxiliary expression. Since every \(x\in D\) satisfies at least one branch, \(D=D^-\cup D^+\). Continue spatial search until every active node is pruned or its certified optimality gap meets the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split the range of a bounded nonlinear expression, rebuild all linked relaxations in each child, and continue until node bounds certify termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Expression Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coverage argument is plausible, but no source supports the exact expression-branching algorithm, its auxiliary-expression treatment, or its termination language. A specific authoritative locator is required.

children.title: Branching Object Selection
children.top_down_role: Structural criteria for choosing between variable-space and expression-space subdivision.

assumptions_latex: A finite set of admissible branching objects is available at the current node.
Each object has a computable score derived only from valid node information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selecting a score maximizer defines a valid branching rule; validity requires exhaustive child domains, while the score affects efficiency rather than correctness.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract validity condition separating object scoring from exhaustive spatial branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node domain \(D\), assign each admissible object \(b\in\mathcal{B}(D)\) a finite score \(S_D(b)\), for example from envelope violation, predicted bound improvement, or accumulated pseudocost information, and choose \(b^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{b\in\mathcal{B}(D)}S_D(b)\). The resulting branching step is valid if its child domains \(D_1,\ldots,D_k\) satisfy \(D\cap F\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^k(D_j\cap F)\), where \(F\) is the original feasible set. Consequently, scoring may change search efficiency, but global correctness depends on exhaustive coverage and valid child bounds, not on which maximizing object is selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the highest-scoring admissible object, but retain correctness by requiring its child domains to cover every parent-feasible point and use valid bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Branching Object Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between scoring efficiency and exhaustive-coverage correctness is mathematically plausible, but the record has no citation for the stated selection principle or examples of scores.

assumptions_latex: The initial bounded domain is a finite rectangle containing the feasible set.
Every generated relaxation supplies a valid lower bound, and incumbent evaluations supply valid upper bounds.
Any infinite refinement sequence reduces the relevant rectangle diameters to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adaptive refinement preserves valid global bounds and concentrates partition cells where their estimated relaxation error or bound impact is largest.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive rectangular refinement for several interacting nonconvex variables.

source_refs.locator: 2.4.2 Convergence of Multivariate Rectangular Partition Methods p. 97

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\mathcal{P}_0\) with the bounding rectangle. At iteration \(k\), solve valid relaxations on active cells \(R\in\mathcal{P}_k\), update the incumbent \(U_k\), discard cells whose lower bound is at least \(U_k-\varepsilon\), and compute refinement scores \(E_k(R)\). Select an active cell of maximal score and split one or more coordinates participating in its nonconvex terms; replace that cell by finitely many children whose union equals it. Rebuild local envelopes and repeat. Output the incumbent when no active cell has lower bound below \(U_k-\varepsilon\); then its objective is globally \(\varepsilon\)-optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly refine the active multivariate cells with greatest estimated impact, rebuild local relaxations, and stop when all cell bounds certify the incumbent gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Multivariate Partitioning

knowledge_statements.title: Spatial Bound-Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic convergence of exhaustive rectangular spatial branch-and-bound under consistent bounding and refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimization of a continuous function \(f\) over a nonempty compact feasible set \(F\). At iteration \(k\), let \(\mathcal{A}_k\) be the finite set of active rectangular nodes, let \(\ell(D)\) be a valid lower bound on \(\min\{f(x):x\in F\cap D\}\), define \(L_k=\min_{D\in\mathcal{A}_k}\ell(D)\), and let \(U_k\) be the best objective value of any feasible point found. Assume child bounds are no smaller than their parent bound, nodes are pruned only by infeasibility or by \(\ell(D)\ge U_k\), every unpruned node eligible for indefinite refinement is selected fairly, every infinite nested branch has diameters tending to zero, and \(\ell(D_r)\) approaches the exact restricted optimum along every such branch \((D_r)\). Then \(L_k\le f^*\le U_k\) whenever active nodes remain, and \(L_k\to f^*\). If, along every infinite unpruned branch, the incumbent mechanism also produces feasible points whose objective values approach the branch's restricted optimum, then \(U_k\to f^*\). At any finite iteration, \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\) certifies global \(\varepsilon\)-optimality of the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For compact problems, monotone valid node bounds, fair exhaustive shrinking refinement, and consistent relaxations make global lower bounds converge to the optimum; consistent feasible recovery also makes incumbent values converge, while a finite bound gap certifies global approximate optimality.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(F\) is nonempty and compact, and the objective \(f\) is continuous.
Node lower bounds are valid, monotone under subdivision, and consistent along shrinking nested boxes.
Refinement is fair and exhaustive, and only infeasibility or valid incumbent-based bounds are used for pruning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The global lower bounds converge to \(f^*\); with consistent feasible recovery, the incumbent upper bounds also converge to \(f^*\), and any finite gap at most \(\varepsilon\) certifies global \(\varepsilon\)-optimality.

children.title: Polyhedral Envelope Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds derived from polyhedral outer descriptions of quadratic terms over bounded domains.

assumptions_latex: The variables have finite bounds \(x_i\in[\ell_i,u_i]\).
Every selected bilinear monomial is represented by an auxiliary variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed affine inequalities are valid polyhedral bounds on each lifted product, and their intersection yields a valid LP lower-bounding relaxation of the nonconvex quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral convex and concave envelope inequalities for bounded bilinear monomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(w_{ij}=x_ix_j\) on \([\ell_i,u_i]\times[\ell_j,u_j]\), impose \(w_{ij}\ge\ell_ix_j+\ell_jx_i-\ell_i\ell_j\), \(w_{ij}\ge u_ix_j+u_jx_i-u_iu_j\), \(w_{ij}\le u_ix_j+\ell_jx_i-u_i\ell_j\), and \(w_{ij}\le\ell_ix_j+u_jx_i-\ell_iu_j\). Their intersection is the convex hull of the bounded bilinear graph. Replacing each lifted product equality by these inequalities, together with the original linear constraints and variable bounds, produces a polyhedral relaxation. For minimization, its optimal value is no greater than the original optimum and is therefore a valid global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Four affine envelope inequalities give the convex hull of each bounded bilinear graph; intersecting them produces a valid polyhedral lower-bounding relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Envelope Bounds

children.title: RLT Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds derived from reformulation-linearization constraints tied to original model relations.

assumptions_latex: Variables satisfy finite bounds \(\ell\le x\le u\).
Every linear constraint is written as \(a_r^{\mathsf T}x-b_r\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting linear program supplies a valid lower bound for every minimization MIQCP represented by the lifted variables.

notation.meaning: lifted variable representing the product of components i and j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-level RLT obtained from products of valid linear inequalities and bound factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Introduce \(X_{ij}\) for every quadratic product \(x_i x_j\). Replace each quadratic occurrence by \(X_{ij}\), and impose every linear inequality obtained by expanding products \((x_i-\ell_i)(x_j-\ell_j)\ge0\), \((u_i-x_i)(x_j-\ell_j)\ge0\), \((x_i-\ell_i)(u_j-x_j)\ge0\), and \((u_i-x_i)(u_j-x_j)\ge0\). Additionally, for each model inequality \(a_r^{\mathsf T}x-b_r\ge0\), multiply it by each nonnegative bound factor \(x_i-\ell_i\) and \(u_i-x_i\), expand, and substitute \(x_i x_j\mapsto X_{ij}\). The intersection of these linear constraints with the lifted model is \(R_{\mathrm{RLT}}\) and contains every lifted feasible point \((x,xx^{\mathsf T})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: RLT linearizes products of bound factors and valid linear constraints. Its lifted polyhedron contains every feasible rank-one point and therefore yields a valid minimization lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: RLT Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The RLT construction and representation kind fit the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the precise first-level system. The ranges of i, j, and r should also be stated explicitly.

children.title: Envelope–RLT Dominance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes determining relative or combined polyhedral bound strength.

assumptions_latex: Both relaxations use the same variable box and the same lifted variables.
The RLT system contains all products of model inequalities with nonnegative bound factors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Full first-level RLT dominates the bound-envelope relaxation, while restricted RLT need not dominate additional problem-specific envelopes.

notation.meaning: relaxation using only product envelopes on the box

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-inclusion comparison under matched lifting and a fixed variable box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each bilinear term \(X_{ij}=x_i x_j\), the four box-product RLT inequalities are exactly its McCormick envelope inequalities; hence, when all such products are generated, \(R_{\mathrm{RLT}}\subseteq R_{\mathrm{env}}\). Consequently, for minimization, \(v(R_{\mathrm{RLT}})\ge v(R_{\mathrm{env}})\). The inclusion can be strict when products of non-bound model inequalities with bound factors add nonredundant cuts. If RLT generation is restricted to only some factors or constraints, or if \(R_{\mathrm{env}}\) includes valid problem-specific convex envelopes absent from the RLT system, no general inclusion follows without separately proving containment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete first-level RLT includes box-product envelopes and may strengthen them using model constraints. With partial RLT or extra problem-specific envelopes, neither dominance claim is automatic.
knowledge_statements.title: Envelope–RLT Dominance Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dominance claim needs a source and qualification: the four McCormick inequalities describe a bilinear term with distinct factor variables, but they are not the exact convex envelope of the square X_ii=x_i^2. The stated all-product inclusion is therefore unreliable as written.

assumptions_latex: The original objective is minimized over a mixed-integer feasible set \(F\subseteq[\ell,u]\).
A convex function \(q_{\mathrm{cvx}}\) satisfies \(q_{\mathrm{cvx}}(x)\le q(x)\) on \([\ell,u]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The convexified relaxation value is a valid global lower bound and is monotone under pointwise improvement of the underestimator.

notation.meaning: original nonconvex quadratic objective or constraint function
convex quadratic underestimator on the current box

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective underestimation on a bounded node domain; analogous substitutions apply to inequality functions with the correct orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replace \(q\) in the objective by \(q_{\mathrm{cvx}}\), relax any integrality or other constraints as desired, and let \(L\) be the resulting minimum. For every \(x\in F\), \(q_{\mathrm{cvx}}(x)\le q(x)\), so \(L\le\min_{x\in F}q(x)\). If two valid convex underestimators satisfy \(q_1(x)\le q_2(x)\le q(x)\) throughout \([\ell,u]\), then their relaxation values satisfy \(L_1\le L_2\); thus pointwise larger valid underestimators yield bounds at least as strong.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing a convex quadratic underestimator over a relaxation gives a global lower bound. A pointwise larger valid underestimator cannot weaken that bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Quadratic Underestimator Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: “Part I Convex Analysis” is not a section/page-level locator for this bound result. Validity also requires the relaxed feasible set to contain F while remaining in a domain where the underestimator is valid, and monotonicity requires both underestimators to be minimized over the same relaxation.

children.title: Conic Global Bounds
children.top_down_role: Global lower bounds obtained from tractable cone-representable quadratic relaxations.

assumptions_latex: The minimization MIQCP is lifted using variables \(X_{ij}\) for quadratic products.
Every imposed conic constraint is valid for all rank-one lifts \((x,xx^{\mathsf T})\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conic relaxation optimum is a valid global lower bound on the original minimization problem.

notation.meaning: a closed convex cone, typically second-order or rotated second-order

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional conic outer relaxations of lifted nonconvex quadratic relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Rewrite every quadratic form as a linear function of \((x,X)\), drop the nonconvex identity \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\), and impose valid constraints of the form \(A(x,X)-b\in K\). Typical rotated-second-order constraints include \(X_{ii}\ge x_i^2\) and \(X_{ii}X_{jj}\ge X_{ij}^2\) with \(X_{ii},X_{jj}\ge0\). Let \(R_K\) denote the resulting conic feasible region. Since each feasible \(x\) of the MIQCP has the feasible lift \((x,xx^{\mathsf T})\in R_K\), minimizing the lifted linear objective over \(R_K\) produces a value no greater than the global optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid second-order or rotated-cone constraints outer-approximate lifted quadratic identities. Minimizing over that conic relaxation gives a global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Conic Global Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conic lifting is mathematically plausible and representation is an appropriate kind, but the precise SOC/rotated-SOC relaxation and its global-bound interpretation have no cited source.

children.title: Semidefinite Global Bounds
children.top_down_role: Global lower bounds obtained from positive-semidefinite lifted relaxations.

assumptions_latex: The minimization MIQCP has quadratic expressions represented linearly in \((x,X)\).
All original feasible points admit the rank-one lift \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The semidefinite relaxation optimum is a valid global lower bound on the MIQCP optimum.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shor-type semidefinite lifting for bounded nonconvex mixed-integer quadratic models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replace each product \(x_i x_j\) by \(X_{ij}\), express all quadratic functions affinely in \((x,X)\), and replace \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) by the moment constraint \[Y:=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\] Add any valid linear equations, bound inequalities, and integrality relaxations desired. Every original feasible point maps to \(Y=(1,x^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}(1,x^{\mathsf T})\succeq0\), so the semidefinite feasible set contains all lifted feasible points. Therefore its minimum lifted objective value is no greater than the original global minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shor lifting replaces the rank-one product matrix by a positive-semidefinite moment matrix. The enlarged feasible set yields a valid global minimization lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Global Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Shor-type SDP lifting is standard and fits the leaf, but no citation with an inspectable locator supports the stated relaxation.

children.title: Conic–Semidefinite Strength Regimes
children.top_down_role: Model structures governing the relative strength of conic versus semidefinite bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic–Semidefinite Strength Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison under a common lift and common affine constraints when the conic constraints are consequences of the positive-semidefinite moment constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_{\mathrm{SDP}}\) and \(R_K\) use the same lifted variables, affine constraints, and linear minimization objective. If every conic constraint defining \(R_K\) is implied by the positive-semidefinite constraint defining \(R_{\mathrm{SDP}}\), then \(R_{\mathrm{SDP}}\subseteq R_K\) and \(v(R_{\mathrm{SDP}})\ge v(R_K)\). If both finite minima are attained, equality holds if and only if some conic-optimal point belongs to \(R_{\mathrm{SDP}}\). The inequality is strict if and only if no conic-optimal point is SDP-feasible. If the models use different lifts or either model contains valid constraints absent from the other, cone type alone establishes no containment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a common lift and common affine constraints, an SDP relaxation dominates a conic relaxation whenever the conic constraints follow from the PSD constraint. Under attainment, their bounds coincide exactly when a conic-optimal solution is SDP-feasible; differing cuts or lifts can remove this ordering.
assumptions_latex: The conic and semidefinite relaxations use the same lifted variables, affine constraints, and linear minimization objective.
Every conic constraint defining \(R_K\) is implied by the positive-semidefinite constraint defining \(R_{\mathrm{SDP}}\).
For the optimizer-based equality characterization, both relaxation minima are finite and attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{SDP}}\subseteq R_K\) and \(v(R_{\mathrm{SDP}})\ge v(R_K)\); under attainment, equality holds exactly when a conic-optimal point lies in \(R_{\mathrm{SDP}}\).

notation.meaning: conic and semidefinite relaxation feasible regions
minimum objective value over a relaxation

children.title: Lagrangian Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds obtained by pricing selected quadratic or linking restrictions.

assumptions_latex: The primal problem is \(p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\le0,\ h(x)=0\}\).
The multiplier satisfies \(\lambda\ge0\), while \(\mu\) is unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every dual value is a valid lower bound, and the best Lagrangian bound is \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda\ge0,\mu}d(\lambda,\mu)\le p^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak Lagrangian duality for a possibly nonconvex mixed-integer minimization problem.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x)+\mu^{\mathsf T}h(x)\) and \(d(\lambda,\mu)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda,\mu)\). For every primal-feasible \(x\) and every \(\lambda\ge0\), \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)\le f(x)\), because \(g(x)\le0\) and \(h(x)=0\). Hence \(d(\lambda,\mu)\le p^*\). Maximizing over admissible multipliers gives the Lagrangian dual bound \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda\ge0,\mu}d(\lambda,\mu)\le p^*\), without requiring convexity or continuous variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing constraints with sign-compatible multipliers gives a lower bound for any minimization problem. Maximizing this bound over multipliers defines the Lagrangian dual bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Bounds

source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

children.title: Surrogate Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds obtained from weighted aggregation of selected model restrictions.

assumptions_latex: The minimization problem has constraints \(g_i(x)\le0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
The aggregation multiplier satisfies \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The surrogate optimum is a valid lower bound on the original optimum, and maximizing it over admissible multipliers gives the surrogate dual bound.

notation.meaning: surrogate relaxation value for multiplier lambda

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative aggregation of inequality constraints in a minimization model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda\ge0\), define the surrogate relaxation \[s(\lambda)=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ \lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x)\le0\}.\] Every point satisfying all inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\) also satisfies their nonnegative aggregation \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x)\le0\). Thus the surrogate feasible region contains the original feasible region and \(s(\lambda)\le p^*\). The best bound in the selected multiplier domain \(\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\}\) is \(s^*=\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}s(\lambda)\le p^*\). Positive rescaling does not change the aggregated constraint, so multipliers may be normalized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative weighted sum of inequality constraints defines a surrogate relaxation. Its optimum is a lower bound, optimized over multiplier directions rather than scales.
knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The surrogate-bound construction and scale invariance are standard and fit the duality leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied for the precise formulation.

children.title: Multiplier Selection Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural considerations governing multipliers used by dualized or aggregated bounds.

assumptions_latex: A dual bound function \(d:\Lambda\to\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\) is evaluated by globally solving its inner relaxation.
The admissible multiplier set \(\Lambda\) has the sign restrictions required for weak duality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Multiplier optimization seeks \(\sup_{	heta\in\Lambda}d(	heta)\); normalization is valid only under positive scale invariance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility, optimization, and normalization rules for Lagrangian and surrogate multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multiplier is bound-valid precisely when it belongs to \(\Lambda\), including nonnegativity for dualized constraints of the form \(g(x)\le0\) and no sign restriction for equalities. Bound selection solves \(\sup_{	heta\in\Lambda}d(	heta)\), or approximately maximizes it while retaining validity at every iterate. For Lagrangian bounds, multiplier magnitude generally affects \(d\) and must not be normalized without justification. For surrogate bounds, if the constraint \(\theta^{\mathsf T}g(x)\le0\) is unchanged under \(\theta\mapsto t\theta\) for \(t>0\), selection may be restricted to a normalization such as \(\theta\ge0\) and \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\theta=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid multiplier signs follow constraint orientation. Lagrangian multipliers generally retain scale, while positively scale-invariant surrogate multipliers may be normalized before optimizing the bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Selection Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between Lagrangian scale sensitivity and surrogate positive-scale invariance is plausible, and condition fits the regime leaf, but the combined multiplier-selection statement lacks cited support.

children.title: Dual Aggregation Gaps
children.top_down_role: Bound losses associated with dualization choices or surrogate aggregation.

assumptions_latex: The primal minimization value \(p^*\) and a best aggregation-based bound \(b^*\) are finite.
Weak duality gives \(b^*\le p^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregation gap is \(\Delta=p^*-b^*\ge0\), and vanishes exactly when the aggregation family attains the primal value.

notation.meaning: best Lagrangian or surrogate aggregation bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gap induced by replacing the original constraint system with a multiplier-parameterized bound family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\Delta=p^*-b^*\). Weak duality implies \(\Delta\ge0\). For a nonconvex or mixed-integer problem, multiplier optimization alone does not imply \(\Delta=0\): aggregation may discard constraint interactions, and the dual function may describe only a convexified value. A concrete strict-gap example is \(p^*=\min\{x:x\in\{0,1\},\ x\ge\tfrac12\}=1\). Dualizing \(\tfrac12-x\le0\) gives \(d(\lambda)=\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}[x+\lambda(\tfrac12-x)]\), whose supremum over \(\lambda\ge0\) is \(\tfrac12\). Thus \(\Delta=\tfrac12\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The aggregation gap is the primal optimum minus the best multiplier bound. Integrality or nonconvexity can leave a positive gap even after exact multiplier optimization.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Aggregation Gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The gap definition and displayed binary strict-gap example are mathematically consistent, and failure_boundary fits the leaf, but neither the general interpretation nor the example has an inspectable citation.

assumptions_latex: A bounded domain \(D\) is partitioned into finitely many sets \(D_k\) with \(D=\bigcup_k D_k\).
Each local relaxation value \(L_k\) is a valid lower bound over \(D_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The partition bound \(L=\min_k L_k\) is globally valid and cannot decrease when every child relaxation strengthens its parent relaxation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bounds formed by spatial partitioning in deterministic global minimization.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Partition Methods on General Convex and Star Sets p. 119

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each cell \(D_k\), let \(L_k\le\inf\{f(x):x\in F\cap D_k\}\), with the convention that an infeasible cell has value \(+\infty\). Because every feasible point belongs to at least one cell, \[L:=\min_k L_k\le\inf_{x\in F}f(x).\] If a cell \(D_k\) is replaced by children \(D_{k1},\ldots,D_{kr}\) covering it, and each child relaxation is at least as tight as the restriction of the parent relaxation, then \(\min_j L_{kj}\ge L_k\). Consequently, refinement cannot weaken the global lower bound under nested local relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum of valid cellwise lower bounds is globally valid. Refining cells monotonically strengthens the bound when child relaxations are nested restrictions of the parent relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Dependent Bounds

source_witnesses.locator: 2.6 Partition Methods on General Convex and Star Sets p. 119

children.title: Quadratic Underestimation Methods
children.top_down_role: Convex underestimators constructed by curvature modification or structured nonconvex decomposition.

assumptions_latex: The box is \(B=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\).
The function \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable on \(B\).
A vector \(\alpha\ge0\) satisfies \(\nabla^2 f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\) for every \(x\in B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The function \(f_{\alpha}\) is convex on \(B\), underestimates \(f\) there, and therefore yields a valid lower bound when minimized over a relaxation of the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Box-dependent diagonal convexification for twice-differentiable nonconvex functions, including indefinite quadratics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[f_{\alpha}(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(x_i-\ell_i)(x_i-u_i).\] Since \((x_i-\ell_i)(x_i-u_i)\le0\) on \(B\), one has \(f_{\alpha}(x)\le f(x)\) throughout \(B\). Moreover, \(\nabla^2 f_{\alpha}(x)=\nabla^2 f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\), so \(f_{\alpha}\) is convex on \(B\). For a quadratic \(f(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\), it suffices that \(Q+\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\). Minimizing \(f_{\alpha}\) over any convex relaxation on \(B\) gives a valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AlphaBB adds nonpositive separable box terms with enough diagonal curvature to make the function convex, producing a box-valid convex underestimator and lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: AlphaBB Convexification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The AlphaBB formula is standard and representation fits the convexification leaf, but no source is supplied. The quadratic specialization requires Q to be symmetric (or use its symmetric part), and the final bound requires a relaxation containing the original feasible set and contained in the box where the underestimator is valid.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(q(x)=x^\top Qx+c^\top x+d\).
\(x\in[l,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\), with finite componentwise bounds.
\(\rho\ge\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(Q)\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline q_\rho(x)\le q(x)\) on \([l,u]\), and \(\underline q_\rho\) is convex.

notation.meaning: separable affine overestimator of the subtracted convex quadratic

standard_field_rationale: spectral shifting and box secants give a standard DC quadratic underestimator.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral DC decomposition with box-secant overestimation of the subtracted convex term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write \(q=g_\rho-h_\rho\), where \(g_\rho(x)=x^\top(Q+\rho I)x+c^\top x+d\) and \(h_\rho(x)=\rho\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2\). Both functions are convex. On \([l,u]\), define \(\overline h_\rho(x)=\rho\sum_{i=1}^n((l_i+u_i)x_i-l_i u_i)\). The secant inequality gives \(h_\rho(x)\le\overline h_\rho(x)\). Consequently, \(\underline q_\rho(x)=g_\rho(x)-\overline h_\rho(x)\) is a convex function satisfying \(\underline q_\rho(x)\le q(x)\) for every \(x\in[l,u]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shift the Hessian to obtain a DC decomposition, then replace the subtracted convex square terms by box secants. The resulting convex quadratic globally underestimates the original quadratic on the box.
knowledge_statements.title: DC Quadratic Underestimation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The spectral shift and box-secant construction is mathematically consistent, and representation is appropriate for this underestimation leaf. No inspectable source with a specific locator is supplied, so the candidate requires sourcing before acceptance.

assumptions_latex: \(B=[l,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a finite box with vertex set \(V(B)\).
\(f:B\to\mathbb R\) is concave on every line segment parallel to a coordinate axis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_V^{\mathrm{cvx}}(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in B\).
review_flags: Exact intended edge-concavity convention requires source confirmation.
standard_field_rationale: successive coordinatewise concavity yields a vertex-supported underestimator.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertex-based convex relaxation for a function concave along every coordinate edge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in B\), define \[f_V^{\mathrm{cvx}}(x)=\min\left\{\sum_{v\in V(B)}\lambda_v f(v):\sum_{v\in V(B)}\lambda_vv=x,\ \sum_{v\in V(B)}\lambda_v=1,\ \lambda_v\ge0\right\}.\] Successive use of concavity along coordinate-parallel segments shows that each point of \(B\) admits a vertex representation whose weighted vertex value does not exceed \(f(x)\). Hence \(f_V^{\mathrm{cvx}}(x)\le f(x)\). The epigraph formulation using variables \(\lambda_v\) is therefore a convex underestimating relaxation suitable for box-based global minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an edge-concave function on a box, minimize the weighted values at box vertices over convex combinations representing the point. This convex vertex formulation underestimates the function.
knowledge_statements.title: Edge-Concave Relaxation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The vertex-value minimum is a valid convex underestimator under coordinatewise concavity, but the intended meaning of edge concavity and the claimed epigraph implementation require an authoritative, specifically located source. Representation otherwise fits the leaf.

assumptions_latex: \(l_i\le x_i\le u_i\) and \(l_j\le x_j\le u_j\) are finite current-node bounds.
\(w_{ij}\) represents the lifted product \(x_ix_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding any violated McCormick inequality cuts off the relaxation point while preserving every point satisfying \(w_{ij}=x_ix_j\).
review_flags: Algorithmic source specific to dynamic MIQCP separation is absent.
standard_field_rationale: dynamic McCormick separation over node bounds is standard.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-local separation of violated McCormick envelopes for lifted bilinear terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a relaxation solution \((\hat x,\hat w)\), evaluate the four McCormick inequalities \(w_{ij}\ge l_i x_j+l_jx_i-l_il_j\), \(w_{ij}\ge u_ix_j+u_jx_i-u_iu_j\), \(w_{ij}\le u_ix_j+l_jx_i-u_il_j\), and \(w_{ij}\le l_ix_j+u_jx_i-l_iu_j\). Add every inequality whose violation exceeds a prescribed tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), optionally prioritizing the largest normalized violations. Recompute these inequalities after branching or bound tightening because their coefficients depend on the current box. Stop when no candidate envelope inequality is violated by more than \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate current-node McCormick inequalities at the relaxation solution, add sufficiently violated envelopes, and regenerate them after bound changes until no material violation remains.
knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Envelope Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The four McCormick inequalities and node-local separation procedure are internally consistent, and algorithm is the correct role. A specific source for dynamic envelope separation in global MIQCP is absent.

assumptions_latex: \(a-Ax\ge0\) and \(b-Bx\ge0\) are valid scalar linear inequalities on the current domain.
\(X\) is intended to represent \(xx^\top\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each separated linearized product inequality is valid for \(X=xx^\top\) and may cut off the current lifted relaxation point.

notation.meaning: linearization operator replacing quadratic monomials by lifted entries

review_flags: A precise RLT separation reference for nonconvex MIQCP is missing.
standard_field_rationale: products of nonnegative valid slacks yield standard RLT inequalities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic separation of lifted inequalities obtained by multiplying valid nonnegative linear slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form candidate products \((a-Ax)(b-Bx)\ge0\) from selected pairs of valid nonnegative slacks. Replace every product \(x_ix_j\) by \(X_{ij}\), obtaining the linear inequality \(\mathcal L_X((a-Ax)(b-Bx))\ge0\). At the current lifted solution \((\hat x,\hat X)\), compute its violation and add inequalities exceeding tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), using normalization to compare differently scaled rows. Candidate pairs may be regenerated after bound tightening or new linear cuts. Terminate the separation round when no tested linearized product is violated beyond \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiply selected pairs of valid nonnegative linear slacks, linearize quadratic monomials with lifted variables, and add the materially violated RLT inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic RLT Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Linearizing products of valid nonnegative affine slacks gives valid RLT inequalities, and the algorithm matches the leaf. The intended candidate-pair scope and dynamic regeneration policy are not supported by an inspectable source.

children.title: Dynamic Conic Separation
children.top_down_role: On-demand separation of violated cone-representable quadratic restrictions.

assumptions_latex: The model contains the valid second-order-cone constraint \(\|Ax+b\|_2\le c^\top x+d\).
\(\hat x\) is a relaxation point with \(\|A\hat x+b\|_2>c^\top\hat x+d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generated affine inequality is valid for the cone and separates \(\hat x\).

notation.meaning: normalized direction at the violating point

review_flags: The cited section supports conic programming generally; the dynamic separation specialization remains provisional.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supporting-hyperplane separation for a violated second-order-cone constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(y=A\hat x+b\). If \(y\ne0\), choose \(u=y/\|y\|_2\); otherwise choose any \(u\) with \(\|u\|_2\le1\). Add the affine cut \(u^\top(Ax+b)\le c^\top x+d\). It is valid because \(u^\top(Ax+b)\le\|Ax+b\|_2\) whenever \(\|u\|_2\le1\). For \(y\ne0\), its violation at \(\hat x\) equals \(\|A\hat x+b\|_2-(c^\top\hat x+d)\). Repeat for cone constraints violated by more than \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a violated second-order-cone constraint, normalize its vector part and add the resulting supporting affine inequality. The cut is cone-valid and separates the violating point.
knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Conic Separation

children.title: Dynamic PSD Separation
children.top_down_role: On-demand separation of violated positive-semidefinite restrictions.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) are lifted relaxation variables.
The intended rank-one relation is \(X=xx^\top\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A negative eigenvector yields a valid linear inequality that separates the non-PSD lifted point.

notation.meaning: eigenvector associated with a negative eigenvalue

review_flags: A direct authoritative locator for dynamic PSD cut separation is absent.
standard_field_rationale: eigenvectors of negative eigenvalues separate the PSD cone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eigenvector separation of the augmented lifted positive-semidefinite constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct \(M(\hat x,\hat X)=\begin{pmatrix}1&\hat x^\top\\ \hat x&\hat X\end{pmatrix}\). If its smallest eigenvalue is below \(-\varepsilon\), choose a corresponding unit eigenvector \(v\) and add \(v^\top M(x,X)v\ge0\). This inequality is affine in \((x,X)\), is valid for every \(M(x,X)\succeq0\), and is violated at \((\hat x,\hat X)\). One may add cuts for several negative eigendirections. Stop when the smallest eigenvalue is at least \(-\varepsilon\), and repeat after the relaxation changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Form the augmented lifted matrix. Each sufficiently negative eigenvalue supplies an eigenvector cut that is linear in lifted variables, valid for the PSD cone, and violated by the current point.
knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic PSD Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A fixed negative eigenvector produces an affine inequality valid for the augmented PSD cone and violated at the current point. The algorithm fits the terminal container, but no authoritative locator supports the dynamic PSD separation procedure.

children.title: Conic–PSD Separation Selection
children.top_down_role: Structural criteria for choosing conic cuts, PSD cuts, or a staged combination.

assumptions_latex: Finite families of violated conic and PSD cuts are available at the current relaxation point.
Each cut has computable violation \(v_k>0\), scale \(s_k>0\), and estimated cost \(c_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure selects a bounded, reproducible subset of valid cuts while retaining the highest-scoring representatives.

notation.meaning: normalized efficacy score of cut k

review_flags: The title denotes an implementation policy with no unique canonical mathematical rule.
A source is required to confirm the intended scoring and diversity criterion.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A score-and-diversity rule for choosing between violated conic and PSD cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every candidate cut \(k\), compute \(\eta_k=v_k/(s_kc_k)\). Discard candidates with \(v_k\le\varepsilon\). Sort the remainder by decreasing \(\eta_k\), then scan the list and accept a cut only if its normalized coefficient vector has absolute inner product at most \(\tau<1\) with every already accepted cut. Stop after accepting \(K\) cuts or exhausting the list. To prevent permanent exclusion of either family, reserve at least one slot for each family having an eligible cut. Output the selected conic and PSD cuts for the next relaxation solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank violated conic and PSD cuts by normalized efficacy and cost, reject nearly parallel duplicates, cap the round size, and reserve representation for each eligible family.
knowledge_statements.title: Conic–PSD Separation Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed score, diversity threshold, family reservation rule, and cut cap define a coherent algorithm, but they are one noncanonical implementation policy among many. A source is needed to establish that this is the intended Conic–PSD Separation Selection rule.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set satisfies the valid disjunction \(D_1\lor D_2\).
\(R_1\) and \(R_2\) are valid convex lifted relaxations under \(D_1\) and \(D_2\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every inequality valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(R_1\cup R_2)\) is valid for the original disjunctive quadratic feasible set.
review_flags: A source fixing the intended disjunctive quadratic cut family is absent.
standard_field_rationale: convex-hull inequalities of valid branch relaxations certify disjunctive validity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity certificate for cuts derived from convexified branch-specific quadratic relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the lifted feasible set and suppose \(F\subseteq(R_1\cap D_1)\cup(R_2\cap D_2)\subseteq R_1\cup R_2\). If an affine inequality \(\alpha^\top x+\langle H,X\rangle\le\beta\) is valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(R_1\cup R_2)\), then it is valid for \(F\). Thus, a separating inequality for a relaxation point outside \(\operatorname{conv}(R_1\cup R_2)\) is a verifiable disjunctive nonconvex quadratic cut. Validity can be checked branchwise by maximizing its left-hand side over each \(R_k\) and confirming values no greater than \(\beta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexify valid lifted relaxations for both sides of a disjunction. Any affine inequality valid on their convex hull is a valid quadratic cut, with validity checkable on each branch.
knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Nonconvex Quadratic Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The branchwise validity argument is mathematically sound and certificate is a defensible role for this validity-focused record. The branch relaxations and intended disjunctive quadratic cut family remain too abstract to identify without a specifically located source.

children.title: Hybrid Discrete–Spatial Search
children.top_down_role: Search organizations coordinating integrality branching, spatial subdivision, and incumbent generation.

assumptions_latex: The active node relaxation has an integer-constrained component \(x_j\) with fractional value \(\hat x_j\).
Spatial branching is deferred while such a fractional integer component is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The children cover the parent feasible set and remove the current fractional value of \(x_j\).
review_flags: No authoritative mixed-integer spatial branch-and-bound locator was supplied.
standard_field_rationale: floor-ceiling branching is exhaustive for integer variables.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hybrid search policy that resolves fractional integer variables before spatial nonconvexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve the current convex relaxation. If some integer-constrained variable satisfies \(\hat x_j\notin\mathbb Z\), select such an index \(j\), for example by pseudocost or strong branching, and create children with \(x_j\le\lfloor\hat x_j\rfloor\) and \(x_j\ge\lceil\hat x_j\rceil\). Repeat integer branching while a fractional integer variable remains. Only after the integer variables are integral, apply spatial branching to a continuous variable participating in a materially violated quadratic relation. Fathom nodes by infeasibility, bound dominance, or a globally feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly apply exhaustive floor-ceiling branching to fractional integer variables. Spatial branching on nonconvex continuous relations begins only after the relaxation solution is integer-feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Integrality-First Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Floor-ceiling branching is exhaustive and removes the current fractional value, while the stated priority policy matches Integrality-First Search. No authoritative mixed-integer spatial branch-and-bound locator is supplied.

assumptions_latex: A current-node relaxation contains a violated lifted relation \(w_{ij}=x_ix_j\) or \(X=xx^\top\).
At least one participating variable has a nondegenerate finite interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The spatial children cover the parent box and reduce the selected nonconvex relaxation error before integrality branching is prioritized.
review_flags: No authoritative locator for this hybrid branching policy was supplied.
standard_field_rationale: exhaustive interval bisection and regenerated envelopes are standard spatial branching operations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hybrid search policy that reduces continuous quadratic relaxation error before enforcing integrality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At the relaxation solution, rank violated quadratic relations by normalized residual, such as \(|\hat w_{ij}-\hat x_i\hat x_j|\). Select a participating variable \(x_k\) and a split point \(t\in(l_k,u_k)\), commonly \(t=\hat x_k\) clipped away from the endpoints. Create children \(x_k\le t\) and \(x_k\ge t\), tighten their bounds, and regenerate bound-dependent envelopes. Continue spatial branching while the maximum quadratic residual exceeds tolerance. Branch on a fractional integer variable only when spatial residuals are sufficiently small or spatial branching is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch first on bounded continuous variables responsible for large lifted quadratic residuals, regenerate tighter envelopes in both children, and defer integrality branching until nonconvex residuals are controlled.
knowledge_statements.title: Spatial-First Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The procedure describes a plausible spatial-first algorithm, but child coverage alone does not establish the unqualified claim that the selected relaxation error is reduced, especially for the general lifted PSD relation. A source is needed to fix the branching measure and supported reduction claim.

assumptions_latex: The current relaxation supplies eligible integer and spatial branching candidates.
Each candidate \(k\) has estimated bound improvement \(\Delta_k\ge0\), processing cost \(c_k>0\), and reliability weight \(r_k\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule selects the reliable candidate with greatest estimated improvement per unit cost, regardless of candidate type.
review_flags: Adaptive mixed branching has multiple non-equivalent scoring policies.
A source is required to identify the intended update and scoring convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Score-based adaptive choice between integer and spatial branching candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each integer or spatial branching candidate \(k\), estimate the two child bound gains \(\Delta_k^-\) and \(\Delta_k^+\) by reliable pseudocosts or limited strong branching. Set \(\Delta_k=\min\{\Delta_k^-,\Delta_k^+\}\) and \(S_k=r_k\Delta_k/c_k\). Select a candidate maximizing \(S_k\) among those with \(r_k\ge r_{\min}\); if none qualifies, probe candidates to update their estimates. Create the exhaustive children associated with the selected candidate, update its statistics after solving them, and repeat until the node is fathomed or certified feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate child bound gains and costs for both integer and spatial candidates, account for estimate reliability, branch on the best score, and update statistics from solved children.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Mixed Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rule is a plausible adaptive mixed-branching algorithm, but it is noncanonical and unsourced. Moreover, maximizing S_k=r_k Delta_k/c_k does not generally select the candidate with greatest estimated improvement per unit cost as the conclusion states, because reliability also changes the ordering.

assumptions_latex: A discrete assignment \(z=\bar z\) satisfying all integrality restrictions is available.
The resulting continuous nonlinear subproblem has explicit bounds and constraints.
The local NLP solver returns a point together with feasibility residuals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only a solver output passing independent feasibility and objective checks is accepted as a globally valid incumbent.
review_flags: The supplied local-global search sources are indirect for MIQCP incumbent interfaces.
standard_field_rationale: fixing discrete variables and independently checking primal feasibility gives a valid incumbent certificate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validated transfer of fixed-integer local NLP solutions into a global MIQCP incumbent pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix the integer variables to \(z=\bar z\), warm-start the continuous variables, and solve the resulting bounded nonlinear program locally. Re-evaluate every original constraint and bound at \((\bar z,\bar y)\) using the global solver's conventions. Accept \((\bar z,\bar y)\) as an incumbent only if all integrality conditions hold exactly or within the prescribed integer tolerance, every primal residual is at most \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\), and the independently recomputed objective improves the incumbent by the required tolerance. A local optimality claim is unnecessary for incumbent validity; verified feasibility and objective value suffice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix an integer assignment, solve the remaining nonlinear problem locally, then independently recheck original constraints, integrality, and objective value. Only a verified feasible improvement enters the global incumbent pool.
knowledge_statements.title: Local NLP Incumbent Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Independent primal and objective checks are sufficient to validate a feasible incumbent without a local-optimality claim. Certificate is defensible for the validation claim, although the leaf title could also support an interface algorithm; a direct MIQCP incumbent-interface source is required to resolve the intended role and tolerances.

children.title: Global Quadratic Domain Reduction
children.top_down_role: Bound-improvement mechanisms integrated with nonconvex quadratic search.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Feasibility Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interval propagation for one quadratic inequality over a node box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the current box be \(B=\prod_{j=1}^n[\ell_j,u_j]\) and let \(q(x)\le 0\) be required. For each variable \(x_i\), compute a rigorous interval lower bound \(L_i(I)\le \inf\{q(x):x\in B,\ x_i\in I\}\). Delete every subinterval \(I\subseteq[\ell_i,u_i]\) satisfying \(L_i(I)>0\); if all of \([\ell_i,u_i]\) is deleted, declare the node infeasible. Repeating these deletions until no bound changes produces a smaller box containing every point in \(B\) feasible for \(q(x)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discard variable subintervals whose rigorous quadratic lower bound is positive. Iteration preserves every feasible point and detects infeasibility when a domain becomes empty.
assumptions_latex: \(q:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is quadratic.
\(L_i(I)\) is a certified lower bound on the stated restricted box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in B:q(x)\le0\}\subseteq B_{\mathrm{reduced}}\subseteq B\).

notation.meaning: certified restricted lower bound for the quadratic

knowledge_statements.title: Optimization-Based Bound Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or safely bounded auxiliary optimization over a node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a node relaxation \(R\supseteq F\), for each selected coordinate \(i\) solve or globally bound \(m_i=\inf\{x_i:x\in R\}\) and \(M_i=\sup\{x_i:x\in R\}\). Replace \([\ell_i,u_i]\) by \([\max\{\ell_i,m_i\},\min\{u_i,M_i\}]\), using outward-safe bounds when the auxiliary problems are not solved exactly. If a new lower bound exceeds a new upper bound, declare the node infeasible. Otherwise output the tightened box; every point of the node-feasible set \(F\) remains inside it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize and maximize selected variables over a valid node relaxation, then intersect the resulting ranges with current bounds without removing feasible points.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\subseteq[\ell,u]\).
Auxiliary extrema are exact or replaced by certified safe bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq\prod_i[\max\{\ell_i,m_i\},\min\{u_i,M_i\}]\).

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

children.title: Dual Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Domain reductions inferred from dual information associated with quadratic relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Bound Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate tightening from feasible dual solutions of relaxation subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a relaxation \(R\), form the auxiliary primal problems \(p_i^-=\inf_{x\in R}x_i\) and \(p_i^+=\inf_{x\in R}(-x_i)\). Obtain dual-feasible solutions with certified dual objectives \(d_i^-\le p_i^-\) and \(d_i^+\le p_i^+\). Update the coordinate bounds by \(\ell_i\leftarrow\max\{\ell_i,d_i^-\}\) and \(u_i\leftarrow\min\{u_i,-d_i^+\}\). Weak duality makes both updates valid even when strong duality fails, provided the reported dual objectives are rigorous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual-feasible objectives for minimizing a variable and its negative provide certified lower and upper variable bounds through weak duality.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\).
The two reported dual points are feasible for valid duals of the auxiliary minimization problems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i\in[\max\{\ell_i,d_i^-\},\min\{u_i,-d_i^+\}]\) for every \(x\in F\).

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Bound Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate bounds obtained by relaxing complicating constraints into a Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R=\{x\in X:g_j(x)\le0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\). For any multiplier \(\lambda\ge0\), define \(L_i^-(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\{x_i+\sum_j\lambda_jg_j(x)\}\) and \(L_i^+(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\{-x_i+\sum_j\lambda_jg_j(x)\}\). Then update \(\ell_i\leftarrow\max\{\ell_i,L_i^-(\lambda)\}\) and \(u_i\leftarrow\min\{u_i,-L_i^+(\lambda)\}\). Maximizing either Lagrangian bound over admissible multipliers strengthens the update but is not required for validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative Lagrange multipliers yield safe coordinate bounds; optimizing the multipliers can strengthen those bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\).
\(g_j(x)\le0\) uses the stated sign convention and \(\lambda_j\ge0\).
The displayed infima are computed or bounded rigorously from below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_i^-(\lambda)\le x_i\le-L_i^+(\lambda)\) for every \(x\in F\).

notation.meaning: simple domain retained in the Lagrangian subproblem
